## 15. Repairs

15.1. All repairs go through the IT desk. The desk keeps a small stock of spare K7s and LP-40s at each site, so that a repair never leaves a rack short.

15.2. Devices are sent to the Korvex service centre in a padded case with a repair note. Nobody opens a device on site.

15.3. A repaired device is rebuilt from Fernguard before it is reissued.

15.4. A device that has been repaired three times in a year is retired.

15.5. The desk reports device faults by type every quarter to the site managers, so that a site whose scanners keep breaking can look at how they are used.

15.6. Repair costs are charged to the site's cost centre. A site that pays for many repairs is not punished for it; it is asked what is going on.

## 16. Leaving Quillfern

16.1. Leavers hand back every device, battery and charger issued to them by name, and the shift lead signs the asset register to show it was received. HR does not issue the leaving papers until the register is signed.

16.2. Sometimes a person who quits keeps their scanner, by accident or otherwise. Anything not returned within two working days of the last shift is recovered from the final settlement at Rs. 18,500 per K7 and Rs. 6,200 per LP-40. The device is then locked and wiped from Fernguard.

16.3. A device returned after the recovery is made is refunded at the same rate, less any repair cost.

16.4. Agency staff never hold a named device, so nothing is recovered from their agencies; their day credentials simply lapse.

16.5. Trainees who leave the Waluj programme early hand their device back to the trainer the same day.

## 6. What stays with us

6.1. Every claim under TPC carries a deductible: a part of each loss that Quillfern bears itself before the insurer pays anything. For 2026–27 the deductible is Rs. 40,000 per consignment. On a loss of Rs. 30,000 the insurer pays nothing; on a loss of Rs. 1,00,000 it pays Rs. 60,000.

6.2. A consignment is one dispatch note. Three pallets on one note make one consignment and carry one deductible. Three notes on one vehicle make three consignments, and each note's loss carries its own deductible.

6.3. Finance books the deductible to the cost centre of the site where the loss happened, or the fleet cost centre where the loss happened on the road. Sites are told their deductible total every quarter.

6.4. Losses below the deductible are still intimated and still recorded. The insurer prices next year's cover on the whole loss record, not only on what it paid, and a record full of gaps is priced as if the gaps were bad news.

6.5. Customers are never told the deductible figure. It is a term of our cover, not of their contract, and quoting it invites an argument about who should bear it.

## 13. Network and data

13.1. K7s connect only to the site's own wireless network, which is separate from the guest and office networks. They do not connect to public or home networks.

13.2. Data on a K7 is encrypted, and the device holds only what the current task needs. Stock records are kept on the warehouse system, not on the device.

13.3. A user who sees a network warning on the screen tells the shift lead and does not tap through it.

13.4. Fernguard keeps a log of every login, every app opened and every update. The log is kept for one year and is read by IT only when there is a reason, such as a missing device or a disputed transaction.

13.5. No customer data leaves the site on a K7. A device taken off site, for a trainee exercise or a repair, is wiped first.

13.6. Wireless coverage is surveyed before a site goes live and again after any racking change. A dead spot found on the floor is reported to the desk with the rack location, and pickers are told to finish the scan at the aisle end rather than wave the device about.

## 2. The cover in one page

2.1. The policy number is TPC/2026/0417 and the policy year runs from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027. Renewal is negotiated by the claims desk with the broker each February.

2.2. The cover applies to goods in transit by road under a Quillfern dispatch note, in owned vehicles and in hired vehicles alike. It covers the goods from the moment loading begins at the origin dock until unloading ends at the destination. It does not cover goods sitting in a building, which are insured under the property policy, and it does not cover air or sea legs booked by the customer.

2.3. Every dispatch is declared to the broker in a monthly return by the 10th of the following month. The return is generated from the dispatch system by the claims desk and checked by Finance. An undeclared dispatch is not automatically uninsured, but the insurer may ask why it was missed, and a pattern of misses can void the cover.

2.4. The premium is charged on the declared value at 0.11 per cent, adjusted at the year end. The most the insurer will pay across all claims in one policy year is Rs. 9 crore. When claims paid pass Rs. 6 crore the broker tells the claims desk, and the desk tells the Finance head the same day.

2.5. Goods are valued at the value written on the dispatch note or the value in the customer's schedule held by Finance, whichever is lower. A value written in a customer's e-mail after a loss is recorded, but it is not the basis of the claim.

## First day driver checklist

Bring licence, Aadhaar copy, bank details, two photos, and any vendor letter if
you are hired-truck staff. At the gate you sign the safety acknowledgement, get
the dispatch note, confirm seal numbers, and check whether the load is pharma,
dairy, frozen, or dry grocery.

Never troubleshoot a telematics device while driving. Park first. If a manager
says "just reach", call Fleet Control and ask them to record the instruction.

## 16. Keeping the file

16.1. Each claim file is kept, complete, for eight years from the date of final settlement or rejection, whichever comes later. Files involving a court case or arbitration are kept until three years after the case ends, if that is longer.

16.2. Scanned files live in the Finance document store under the TPC26 number. Paper originals are boxed by policy year and kept in the Finance archive room.

16.3. Physical evidence — seals, logger files, damaged packaging — is kept until the claim is closed, then for one more year, and is then disposed of with the desk lead's signature.

16.4. A file is never weeded to save space. If storage runs short, the desk lead asks Finance for more.

## 17. Review

17.1. The IT infrastructure lead reviews this policy every March and after any loss of data, any serious security warning or any change of device model.

17.2. Site managers and shift leads send suggested changes to the IT desk at any time.

17.3. A revised policy is issued with a short note of what changed, and the Fernguard settings are changed on the same day, so that the policy and the devices never disagree.

17.4. When a site opens, the IT desk walks its shift leads through this policy on a live device before go-live, and the shift leads walk their teams through it in the first week.

## 1. Parties and how to read this

1.1. The parties are Quillfern Cold Logistics Pvt. Ltd. ("Quillfern") and
Saptagiri Foods Pvt. Ltd. ("the customer"), a maker of frozen parathas, samosas
and snacks with a factory at Chakan.

1.2. The agreement began on 1 April 2025 and runs until either side ends it under section 10.

1.3. Amendment 1 took effect on 1 October 2025 and changed the payment terms.
Amendment 2 took effect on 1 April 2026 and changed the liability cap. Both are
folded into the text below and listed in section 15.

1.4. Clause numbers here follow this consolidation, not the original agreement.
A clause quoted from the signed record carries its original number.

## 4. Behind door 3

4.1. The cell behind D3 is BC-1, a blast cell with an air temperature of -35 C
and room for six pallets. It exists because brand owners do not always send
stock as cold as their paperwork says, and a frozen store is not built to pull
warm stock down; it is built to hold cold stock cold.

4.2. Every inbound pallet is probed at the dock: one carton from the middle of
the pallet, probe into the product core. Anything with a core warmer than minus 12 on the arrival probe goes behind door 3 first, whatever the paperwork says.

4.3. The target in the cell is a core of minus 18. It gets six hours from the moment the doors close. A load that has not reached target by then is reported to QA and held, and the customer is told the same day.

4.4. Stock that comes out of the cell is probed again before it goes into FC-A,
and both readings are written on the inbound sheet with their times.

4.5. The cell is never used as overflow storage, however busy the night. A
pallet parked in the cell because FC-A is full blocks the next soft arrival,
and the next soft arrival then sits on the dock warming further.

4.6. The cell's fans put a hard frost on cartons that sit too close to the coil.
Pallets are placed on the painted floor marks and nowhere else.

4.7. Whether cell time is charged depends on the customer's contract, not on
this handbook. The shift lead records the door-closing and door-opening times on
the cell log so that the office can apply whatever the contract says.

4.8. The cell was enlarged from four to six pallet places in March 2026. The two
extra places took space from the apron, which is why the apron now holds nine
vehicles and not eleven.

## 10. Ending the agreement

10.1. Either side may bring it to an end by giving 120 days' written notice.

10.2. Either side may end it at once if the other fails to pay, or fails to
perform a material obligation, and does not put it right within 30 days of a
written demand.

10.3. On ending, Quillfern returns the customer's stock to Chakan or to a place
the customer names in Pune, at the customer's cost, within 15 days.

## 14. Training and coaching for drivers

14.1. Every new owned-reefer driver rides two supervised runs with an experienced
driver before driving alone. One of the two is a night run.

14.2. The supervised runs cover the cab card, the takeover walk-round, the seal
routine, the red sleeve, the gate checklist for pharma runs and the way to speak
to Fleet Control on the phone. The experienced driver signs the new driver's
training sheet at the end of each run.

14.3. Telematics coaching calls are held within two working days of an alert, as
the policy says. The coach asks what happened before saying anything about what
should have happened.

14.4. Drivers who complete a year with no safety non-conformance receive a
certificate from the Fleet head, presented at the Nagpur driver meeting. The
certificate carries no money and is not tied to arrival times.

14.5. The Nagpur driver meeting is held on the last Saturday of each month in
the driver rest room. Attendance is paid duty time. Drivers on the road that day
receive the notes on their phone.

## 10. Hired trucks and their drivers

10.1. A hired-truck vendor is on the approved list before the first booking, and
each of its drivers signs the policy acknowledgement at the gate before loading.

10.2. Hired trucks carry their own fuel. Quillfern fuel cards are never given to
hired drivers.

10.3. Hired trucks are sealed with cable seals. Their drivers are shown the seal
routine at the gate by the shift lead.

10.4. A hired truck without a working temperature display is not loaded with
cold-chain stock, whatever the vendor promises about a repair on the way.

10.5. Vendors are reviewed every quarter on arrival times, refused loads,
exceptions and any safety concern raised by a DC.

## 10. Doors, curtains and ice

10.1. Every door into FC-A and the cell is a rapid-roll door with a strip curtain
behind it. A door that does not close fully within 20 seconds of a vehicle
passing is reported to the shift lead.

10.2. The door heaters keep the frame of each freezer door from icing. The
morning shift lead checks each heater light at the start of the shift and logs
any that is out.

10.3. Ice on the floor in front of a freezer door is chipped and cleared at once,
not left for the next shift. The ice is swept into the drain channel outside,
never left in the anteroom to melt.

10.4. A strip curtain with a torn strip is replaced within a week. The spare
strips are in the store cage in the anteroom.

10.5. The dock seals at D4 to D6 are checked by the guard each evening. A seal
that does not meet the van body lets warm air into the anteroom and frost onto
the picking cartons.

## 5. Temperatures

5.1. The customer's products are kept at -18 C or colder in storage and in
transit.

5.2. The customer pre-cools each trailer before loading at Chakan and sends the
pre-cool record with the trailer.

5.3. Product that turns up above minus 12 is brought down to temperature at the cross-dock, and that work is invoiced to the customer.

5.4. Quillfern is not liable for product damage caused by temperatures before
handover. Each party may inspect the other's temperature records for its
stock.

# East Coast Region Operating Plan 2026-28

## 1. Why the east coast

1.1. Quillfern has grown along an arc from the west into the centre of the country, and its customers have asked for years to be served on the east coast as well. Three things decided the matter in 2025. A shrimp exporter in the Godavari delta offered a five-year volume commitment if we would hold its frozen stock near the port. A vaccine maker opening a fill-finish line near Bhubaneswar asked for a cold distribution partner inside the state. And the growth of organised food retail in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha meant that frozen and chilled lanes we were already being asked to quote would pay for themselves.

1.2. This plan describes the region we are building: one distribution centre at Visakhapatnam, which people on the ground call Vizag, and one inland satellite at Bhubaneswar. It covers the calendar, space, people, power, weather, port work, fleet, money and the measures by which the region will be judged in its first two years.

1.3. It is written for the region's own managers, for the head-office teams who support them, and for the board, which approved the investment in March 2026. It replaces the outline written in 2025, which was prepared before the site was chosen.

1.4. Company-wide procedures apply in the region from the first day. Nothing in this plan relaxes a temperature rule, a driving rule or a quality rule because the region is new.

# East Coast region: outline plan for site selection

Prepared before the Visakhapatnam plot was chosen, to size the investment for
the board's first look.

## 11. After the stock has left

11.1. Responsibility for a batch does not end at the dispatch bay. The store must be able to find every unit it has handled, and it must deal properly with what comes back.

11.2. Twice a year, in March and September, the store runs a mock recall on a batch chosen by the RP without warning. The exercise starts when she names the batch to the shift QA officer. Every unit of the chosen batch must be found and named — on a shelf, on a vehicle or at a consignee — inside four hours of the exercise starting. The result, with the time taken and any unit that could not be found, goes to the customer who owns the batch.

11.3. Hospitals and distributors send product back for many reasons — over-ordering, a ward closing, a wrong delivery — and none of those reasons makes it fit to be resold. Nothing returned goes back into saleable stock unless it comes back within 72 hours of delivery, with an unbroken logger record from our hands to the consignee's and back, and the Responsible Person signs the release; everything else is destroyed. Returned product waits in the quarantine cage while the decision is made.

11.4. A real recall, as opposed to a practice one, is run by the customer. The store's part is to stop dispatch of the batch at once, list every unit it holds and every unit it has sent, and hold any returned units in quarantine until the customer instructs.

11.5. Complaints from hospitals about a product's quality are passed to the customer the same day. The store does not reply to the complaint itself, and does not offer an opinion on it.

## 14. Risks we can see

14.1. The anchor customer is a single exporter. If Godavari Aqua's export market falls, the frozen block is half empty. The plan reduces that risk by signing at least two more frozen customers before the end of 2027.

14.2. Storms may close the region for days at a time. Section 9 sets the response.

14.3. Skilled refrigeration technicians are scarce on this coast. Two places on each intake of the company's technician programme are reserved for people from the region, who return to it on completion.

14.4. The vaccine maker's start date may slip. Pharma space is not filled with food while it waits; it stays empty.

14.5. Port congestion may hold containers at the DC longer than planned. The container plugs in section 10 are the buffer.

## 18. Things left out on purpose

18.1. The satellite does not store medicines and does not unload them. Pharma stock for Odisha customers either travels direct from the DC in a sealed vehicle that passes through the satellite's yard without opening, or is delivered by the DC's own vehicle. No passive shipper, no cross-dock exception and no customer's urgency changes this.

18.2. The region does not handle live seafood, fresh fish on ice or any product that is not packed and labelled.

18.3. The region does not offer customs clearance as a service. The exporter's own agent clears its goods; we provide the space and the supervision of stuffing.

18.4. The DC does not open a retail counter or sell surplus stock locally.

## 12. People, gowns and hands

12.1. Every person who enters a product zone has completed the store's induction, which covers this manual, gowning, hand hygiene and what to do when an alarm sounds. Visitors are escorted and do not touch product.

12.2. Gowning is done in the gowning room: a clean overcoat, a hair cover, and for the chambers a freezer jacket from the rack. Outdoor shoes stay on the outer side of the bench.

12.3. Nobody eats, drinks, chews or smokes in a product zone. Medicines of one's own are kept in the locker room, never in a pocket.

12.4. A person with a stomach upset, an open wound on the hands or a skin infection tells the shift QA officer before starting work and is given work away from open product.

12.5. Training is refreshed every year and whenever a procedure the person uses changes. A person whose training has lapsed does not work in a product zone until it is refreshed, however short-staffed the shift.

12.6. Training records show the date, the trainer, the procedure revision and a short test result. A signature alone is not a training record.

- First customer stock: September 2026.
- Chilled pallet positions: 2,000. Frozen pallet positions: 1,200.
- Staff at go-live: 58.
- Owned reefers: 10.

## 11. Pairing

11.1. Each LP-40 label printer is paired over Bluetooth to one K7, and the pairing is recorded against both asset numbers in Fernguard.

11.2. Pickers sometimes need to hook a printer up to a different scanner when theirs has gone flat or been swapped. Only a shift lead may move one to another K7, and the change is logged in Fernguard. A printer paired without a log entry prints labels nobody can trace to a user.

11.3. A printer whose labels come out faint or skewed is cleaned with the head-cleaning pen kept in the rack, and returned to the desk if that does not cure it.

11.4. Label stock is loaded only from the sealed rolls held at the rack. Rolls left open on a dock pick up dust that scratches the print head.

11.5. A printer that will not pair after two attempts is put aside with a note and the shift lead uses the rack spare.

## 2. The kit

2.1. The K7 is a rugged Android terminal with a built-in barcode reader, a 5-inch screen, a hot-swap battery and a wrist strap. It is rated for drops of 1.8 m onto concrete and for use in rain, but not for long use in a freezer (section 10).

2.2. The LP-40 is a belt-clip thermal printer for pallet and carton labels. It pairs with one K7 over Bluetooth.

2.3. Each K7 sits in a charging cradle when not in use. Cradles are mounted on cradle racks of ten, one rack per shift area, and each rack holds two spare K7s that belong to the rack rather than to a person.

2.4. Every device carries an asset label with its number, and Fernguard knows every device by its serial number. An asset label that is peeling is replaced by the IT desk, not taped over.

2.5. No other phone, tablet or scanner may be used for stock work at these sites. A customer's own scanner brought by an auditor is used only to read, never to transact.

2.6. The fleet at the date of this revision is 118 K7s and 34 LP-40s across the four sites, with the numbers per site held in the asset register. The register, not this policy, is the place to check a count.

# Handheld Terminal and Mobile Device Policy

## 1. Purpose and reach

1.1. This policy governs the rugged terminals, label printers and charging cradles issued to the sites opened since 2025: the pharma store at Changodar, the Visakhapatnam DC and its Bhubaneswar satellite, and the engineering training workshop at Waluj. Those sites run on the Korvex K7 terminal and the LP-40 printer, managed centrally from the Fernguard console. Sites that use other equipment are not covered here.

1.2. It is written for everyone who is issued a K7 or uses one on a shift — pickers, receiving clerks, QA officers, shift leads, drivers' mates and trainees — and for the IT staff who look after the fleet. Floor staff rarely say "terminal"; they say scanner or gun, and both words mean a K7 in this policy.

1.3. The policy exists because a K7 is three things at once: a stock-control tool, a key to customer data and an expensive piece of hardware that is easy to put down and forget. Each section below deals with one or more of those.

1.4. Revision 2 replaces the quick rules written for the 2025 pilot, when twenty K7s were tried at the Waluj workshop before the fleet was bought. Where a figure changed, the section says so.

1.5. MDM in this policy means Fernguard and nothing else. No other management tool is installed on a K7, and the IT desk does not accept a vendor's offer to add one.

## 19. Office consumables and general supplies

19.1. Stores also holds the everyday supplies the sites run on: printer paper,
toner, pens, markers, stretch wrap, packing tape, pallet labels, torch batteries
for the gate cabins and cleaning materials.

19.2. These are issued against a signature like everything else, but in larger
units: a ream, a box, a roll. Stores does not count pens.

19.3. Stretch wrap and packing tape are issued to the dock teams by the carton at
the start of each week. A dock that runs out before the week ends asks Stores,
and Stores notes which dock and why.

19.4. Pallet labels are printed by the dock teams from Dockwise. Stores holds the
blank label rolls and the spare printer ribbons, and keeps two spare label
printers in the cage for a swap.

19.5. Cleaning materials are issued to the housekeeping contractor against its
own signature. The contractor's staff do not take anything from the cage
themselves.

## 10. Counting

10.1. Stores counts seals, sleeves and instruments every Friday, and everything
else at the month end.

10.2. A count is done by two people, one of whom did not issue anything that
week.

10.3. At the Friday count the logger shelf is checked by date: a logger whose
last bench check is more than 90 days old is moved to the QA tray, and a logger
whose battery date shows more than 24 months is flagged, but nothing in the
store count replaces what the QA bench decides.

10.4. Differences are written up the same day and sent to Nalini Patil. A
difference in seals or loggers is reported to QA and Fleet Control as well.

10.5. Guwahati and Coimbatore cages send their counts to the Nagpur store by
email on the first working day of the month.

## 5. Red sleeve packets

5.1. Stores holds red sleeve packets empty. QA makes each packet up, including a
spare logger checked at the bench, before it is issued.

5.2. A made-up packet comes back to Stores from QA sealed with a tamper label.
Stores does not open it.

5.3. Stores issues made-up packets to DCs and to reefer cab lockers against a
signature. A packet returned unused and unopened goes back on the shelf; a
packet returned opened goes to QA to be made up again.

5.4. Stores keeps at least ten made-up packets at Nagpur at all times. When the
stock falls to ten, Stores tells QA in writing.

5.5. Packets ordered under the red sleeve project are recorded against that
project's budget line, not against the Stores consumables line.

## 8. Heavy days on the road

8.1. The insurer's exposure on any single vehicle is capped. The most it will pay for all goods on one vehicle on one trip is Rs. 1.2 crore, however many consignments are on board.

8.2. A full vaccine load easily goes past that figure, and so does a frozen load of premium seafood. Any dispatch whose total declared value on one vehicle is above Rs. 1.2 crore is declared to the broker in writing at least 48 hours before the vehicle leaves. The broker then gets the insurer's agreement to a higher figure for that trip, or tells us to split the load.

8.3. Fleet planners check the declared value of every pharma critical and every high-value frozen load when they build the week's plan, and send the list of trips over the figure to the claims desk on Thursday.

8.4. A trip that goes over the figure without a declaration is still covered up to Rs. 1.2 crore. Anything above that is uninsured, and the site manager who allowed the load explains why in writing.

8.5. Splitting a load costs a second vehicle and a second crew. Planners should prefer splitting to asking for a higher figure only where the second vehicle is already on the road; the broker's higher figure usually costs less than an empty run.

## 14. Money in

14.1. The insurer pays an agreed claim within 30 days of receiving the surveyor's final report or, for a desk-assessed claim, within 30 days of receiving the complete file. On day 31 the desk asks the broker to chase, and on day 45 the desk lead writes to the broker's branch head.

14.2. Payment comes to Quillfern's account, never to the customer's, even when the customer's goods were lost.

14.3. Finance books the expected recovery as a receivable when the claim is agreed, not when it is intimated, and writes off any part the insurer refuses once the desk lead has decided not to dispute it.

14.4. Credit notes to customers are not tied to insurance money. A customer is paid what the contract says, when the contract says, whether or not our own claim has succeeded.

14.5. Disputes with the insurer about the amount go through the broker first. The policy's arbitration clause is used only with the Finance head's approval.

## 17. Changes to this manual

17.1. Revision 1 (September 2025) was issued when the store opened. Revision 2 (December 2025) added the generator test after a power failure in the first month. Revision 3 (May 2026) changed several frequencies and limits after the store's first full season, and recorded the reasons beside each change.

17.2. The QA lead reviews this manual every April and after any critical deviation, failed customer audit or change to the building. The RP approves each revision.

17.3. Staff send suggested changes to the QA lead at any time. Each suggestion gets an answer, whether or not it is taken up.

17.4. A revised manual is issued with a one-page note of what changed. Every person who works in a product zone signs that they have read the note within a week of issue.

## 17. What changed from the 2025 cover

17.1. The 2025–26 cover was placed with the same insurer on different terms, and its summary note is withdrawn. Staff who learned the old figures should unlearn them.

17.2. The deductible rose, the intimation window shortened, the machinery-stoppage threshold came down, the single-vehicle figure went up, and the survey threshold went up. The current figures are in sections 5 to 9 of this procedure and nowhere else.

17.3. SRCC cover was added by endorsement for the first time.

17.4. The desk lead reviews this procedure each February, before renewal, and issues a revision whenever the policy terms change.

## 1. Nagpur DC, also written NGP hub

1.1. Book Nagpur slots in Dockwise before 15:00 on the previous day. The old
16:00 cut-off moved because the ammonia plant defrost window moved.

1.2. Dock assignment: pharma uses dock 4, dairy uses docks 1 and 2, frozen food
uses dock 5, and dry grocery uses dock 6. Dock 6 was added in January 2026 and
does not appear on the wiki page.

1.3. No unloading is planned between 12:40 and 13:20 for the daily ammonia plant
defrost check.

1.4. Late arrival is cancelled automatically in Dockwise after 20 minutes for
dairy and after 30 minutes for dry grocery. Pharma and frozen bookings are never
auto-cancelled; they go to holding lane B and the shift lead is called.

## 5. Taking a booking

5.1. A booking needs the product class, the quantity in the unit the rate card
uses, the pickup and delivery points, the earliest and latest delivery time, and
the name of the person who will receive.

5.2. The agent checks that the booked vehicle can carry the product class. RF-120
is frozen only; RF-119 takes pharma only with a passive shipper; RF-118 takes
pharma and dairy but never frozen.

5.3. The agent books the dock through Dockwise for Nagpur, Guwahati and
Coimbatore alike. A phone slot at Guwahati is confirmed in Dockwise the next
working day.

5.4. Pharma critical bookings that would need a night segment are passed to
Fleet Control before they are confirmed to the customer, because a night pharma
run needs two named drivers.

5.5. A booking the customer changes after 15:00 the day before is treated as a
new booking.

## 6. Spare instruments

6.1. Stores holds spare hand-held probes and spare USB loggers for issue, but
does not decide whether an instrument is fit to use. The sticker, put on by QA,
decides that.

6.2. A spare logger's battery is replaced by Stores after 24 months on the
shelf, whatever the logger's sticker says, and the logger then goes back to the
QA bench before it can be issued.

6.3. An instrument with a yellow sticker may be issued. An instrument with a red
sticker or red tape is never issued and goes back to QA.

6.4. Stores keeps a list of every instrument by its prefix number and the date
of its last in-house check, so that QA can see what is due.

6.5. Instruments sent to the external lab are packed by QA and handed to the
courier by Stores. Stores records the date they left and the date they came
back.

## 1. What Stores does

1.1. Stores buys nothing on its own authority. It raises a request against a
purchase order that Finance has approved, receives the goods, holds them, issues
them against a signature and counts them.

1.2. The Nagpur main store keeps the stock for Nagpur and sends stock to
Guwahati and Coimbatore by courier or on a scheduled vehicle. The Guwahati and
Coimbatore cages hold only what their DC uses in about a month.

1.3. Every item issued is signed for by the person who takes it. An item that
leaves Stores without a signature is counted as lost at the next count.

1.4. Stores does not lend. An item taken for a job is either used, returned or
written off, and each of those is recorded.

## 2. Grace periods

| class | grace | note |
|---|---|---|
| pharma critical | 20 min | call QA and shift lead; check the red sleeve before moving to dock 4 |

## 3. Receiving goods

3.1. Goods are received against the purchase order and the delivery note, and
counted before the delivery note is signed. A short delivery is written as short
on the delivery note in front of the supplier's driver.

3.2. Temperature-sensitive consumables, such as conditioned gel packs, are not
received by Stores. They go directly to the QA room.

3.3. Calibrated instruments are received by Stores and passed unopened to the QA
bench on the same day. Stores does not open an instrument box to check it.

3.4. Damaged goods are photographed, set aside and reported to Finance before the
supplier's driver leaves, where that is possible.

17.1. A new agent spends the first two weeks listening to calls with an

17.4. The customer service lead meets each new agent at the end of their first
month and again at three months.

the night shift lead holds the emergency cupboard key, as in section 2.

23.2. Questions about whether an item is fit to use go to QA. Questions about
whether an item may be bought go to Finance. Stores answers questions about
where an item is and how many are left.

## 5. What this document does not do

5.1. It does not set any temperature limit, staging allowance, or excursion
definition. Those live in QCL-QA-SOP-17 and a dock booking never overrules them.

5.2. It does not change driver hours. A slot that cannot be met inside the
driver's remaining hours is rebooked, not driven to.

## 4. Coimbatore DC

4.1. Use the south gate for reefers. Avoid Temple Street between 07:45 and 08:30.

4.2. Frozen loads are placed before lunch. Coimbatore joined Dockwise on
1 February 2026 with Guwahati.

## 10. On live units

10.1. On a live unit — a working reefer, a cold room with stock in it, a customer's freezer — an apprentice is never the only pair of hands. Live means anything holding product or able to start without warning, and it is the real kit apprentices are here to learn on.

10.2. One qualified technician supervises at most three apprentices on live equipment. On a pharma chamber the ratio is one to one.

10.3. Night work is part of the job later, not at first. No apprentice is put on a night roster before month nine, even with a supervisor. From month nine an apprentice may be rostered at night with a qualified technician on the same job.

10.4. Apprentices never isolate, lock out or restore power on their own until they have passed the electrical module, and never on a pharma chamber during the programme.

10.5. An apprentice who is asked to do something on a live unit that this curriculum forbids says no, and tells the mentor the same day. Saying no is never held against the apprentice.

## 3. Planning a week of duty

3.1. Planners build the week's duty on Thursday for the following Monday to
Sunday. Each driver's weekly rest is placed first, then night segments, then
day runs.

3.2. The limits the plan must respect are in the Driver Hours and Road Safety
Policy. A plan that meets them only if nothing goes wrong does not meet them.

3.3. A lane with a qualification record is planned with that record open, so
that its relief point, its pre-cool hold time and any two-driver condition are
on the plan and not in someone's memory.

3.4. Festival shuttle rosters with split rest are planned only after the Fleet
head has approved the roster in writing, and only for the festival named.

3.5. The plan is published to drivers by Friday noon. A driver who sees a
problem with his week tells Fleet Control on Friday, not on the morning of the
run.

3.6. Leave requests go to the planner by the 20th of the previous month. Late
leave is granted where cover exists, and cover is never found by stretching
another driver's hours.

## 6. Before the first charge

6.1. No apprentice touches a refrigerant charge without the gas-handling certificate, the "gas ticket" in workshop talk. Recovering, charging, venting and leak-testing all count as touching a charge. Until then apprentices may watch, read gauges and wire controls.

6.2. The certificate is sat at the end of month four, and an apprentice who fails it may resit once, in month five. An apprentice who fails the resit leaves the programme, because there is no job on the floor for someone who may not handle refrigerant.

6.3. The certificate is examined by an outside body recognised for refrigerant handling. Quillfern pays the examination fee for the first sitting and the resit.

6.4. The workshop teaches the recovery of every refrigerant used at the sites, including the natural refrigerants on the newer plant, and the reasons why venting is never acceptable.

6.5. An apprentice who holds the certificate carries the card on every job, and a site may turn away an apprentice who cannot show it.

## 5. Money

5.1. Every apprentice is paid a monthly stipend, not a wage, and it rises once, when the apprentice moves from the workshop to the floor. Pay is credited to the apprentice's own bank account on the last working day of the month.

5.2. The stipend is Rs. 14,000 a month for months one to six and Rs. 16,500 from month seven; the 2025 outline gave a flat Rs. 12,000. The rise recognises that floor months are longer and often away from home.

5.3. Apprentices placed at a site away from Waluj receive a lodging allowance and their travel to the site and back at the start and end of the placement. The allowance is set by the site and paid with the stipend.

5.4. Overtime is not paid to apprentices, because apprentices do not work overtime. An apprentice kept beyond the shift by an emergency is given the time back the next day.

5.5. No apprentice is bonded. Nobody repays anything for leaving the programme early or for taking a job elsewhere after it, and nobody is asked to sign a promise to stay.

## 5. People and shifts

5.1. The site manager is Prakash Jadhav. He is the escalation contact for the
site at any hour and the only person who may approve a change to the van plan
after it has been published.

5.2. The site works three shifts: 06:00 to 14:00, 14:00 to 22:00 and 22:00 to
06:00. Inbound trailers are mostly unloaded on the night shift; outbound vans are
loaded from 04:30 on the morning shift.

5.3. Each shift has a shift lead. Swati Kulkarni leads the morning shift, Imran
Shaikh the afternoon shift, and the night shift lead is named on the weekly
roster on the canteen board, because two people share it.

5.4. Floor labour is supplied under contract by Sai Kripa Manpower. Contract
staff are inducted by the shift lead before their first shift and wear the
green bibs; Quillfern staff wear blue.

5.5. Nobody works inside FC-A for more than 45 minutes without a 15-minute warm
break in the canteen. The shift lead keeps the break board and moves names on
it, not the workers themselves.

5.6. Freezer suits, gloves and boots are issued to named people. A worker without
a suit does not enter FC-A, even for a minute to fetch one carton.

5.7. Overtime is approved by the site manager in advance. A shift that cannot
finish a trailer leaves it for the next shift with a handover note; it does not
stay on past the end of shift to finish it.

## 14. Safety on the floor

14.1. The safety rules of the site always apply. Where a site rule and this curriculum differ, the stricter one wins.

14.2. Apprentices wear their safety gear on every job, including short ones.

14.3. Refrigerant cylinders are carried upright and strapped in vehicles. Apprentices never carry a cylinder in a bus or on a motorcycle.

14.4. Brazing is done only with a permit and a fire watch, at the workshop and on site alike.

14.5. Any injury, however small, is reported to the mentor the same day and written in the site's accident book.

## 11. Crashes, near misses and police stops

11.1. After any crash, however small, the driver makes the vehicle and the road
safe, calls emergency services if anyone is hurt, and then calls Fleet Control.

11.2. The driver does not move the vehicle unless the police tell him to or it
is a danger where it stands. Photographs of the scene are taken if it is safe.

11.3. The driver is relieved from further driving until Fleet Control records a
fitness-to-continue decision, as the policy requires.

11.4. A near miss is reported the same day, in the driver's own words. Near-miss
reports are not used to discipline the driver who reports them.

11.5. A police stop that is not a crash and not an inspection of the load, such
as a document check, is noted in the driver call log with the time and place.

## 10. Emergency cold for a customer's kitchen

10.1. Restaurant chains sometimes ask for emergency dry-ice packing when their
own freezer fails. Customer service takes the request; the DC decides whether it
can be done.

10.2. The agent does not promise a time. The DC tells the agent when the packing
can be ready, and the agent passes that on.

10.3. Emergency dry-ice packing is billed at a minimum of 10 kg per request,
whatever smaller quantity the kitchen asks for, and the per-kg price is the one
on the rate card in force.

10.4. Dry ice is never sent in a customer's own car unless the customer's driver
signs the dry-ice safety note at the gate. Customer service sends the note to
the customer with the confirmation.

10.5. Pharma customers are not offered dry-ice packing as an emergency measure.

## 8. Dry ice supply

8.1. Stores places the standing order for dry ice at Nagpur. Vidarbha Gases
delivers 120 kg on Monday and Thursday mornings, and extra deliveries are
ordered by Stores on the shift lead's request.

8.2. Stores does not hold dry ice in the store. The delivery goes straight to
the dry-ice chest, where the shift lead signs the delivery note.

8.3. At the weekly count Stores records the kg delivered, the kg signed out on
QCL-F-26 and the kg left in the chest, and the difference is recorded as
sublimation loss.

8.4. Guwahati and Coimbatore order their own dry ice from their local suppliers,
and send Stores the delivery notes monthly.

## 8. Carbon dioxide on board

8.1. Dry ice may be put into a frozen body only at a Quillfern DC dock or in a
customer's secure yard with Fleet Control's approval. No dry ice is added to a
body between DCs, at a relief point, at a toll plaza or at a fuel stop.

8.2. A frozen body running warm on the road is driven to the nearest Quillfern
DC or approved customer yard, within the driver's remaining hours, and the load
is protected there.

8.3. Dry ice never travels in the cab, whatever the distance. A driver who is
handed pellets for the cab refuses them.

8.4. A driver who opens a body in which dry ice has been placed stands back from
the open doors and keeps others back until the air has cleared.

8.5. Dry ice put into a body at a dock is written on the dispatch note with the
kg, so that the receiver knows to open the doors with care.

# Stores and Consumables Standard

How Stores receives, holds and issues the consumables that cold-chain work runs
on: seals, red sleeve packets, spare loggers, gel packs, dry ice, protective
equipment and forms. It covers the main store at Nagpur and the smaller stores
cages at Guwahati and Coimbatore. It does not say how any of these items is used
on the job; the documents that govern their use do that.

## 9. Protective equipment

9.1. Stores issues cryogenic gloves, face shields, freezer suits, safety shoes,
high-visibility vests and hearing protection against a signature.

9.2. Freezer suits are issued to named people, not to a shift. A suit that no
longer closes properly is returned and replaced.

9.3. Cryogenic gloves and face shields for dry-ice work are not personal issue.
They hang on the rack beside each chest and are replaced by Stores when damaged.

9.4. Safety shoes are replaced once a year, or sooner if the sole is split.

9.5. Hired-truck drivers are issued a high-visibility vest at the gate and return
it at the gate.

## 4. Giving a customer a price

4.1. Agents quote from the rate card in force on the day of the quotation, and
write the rate card's effective date on the quotation.

4.2. BharatVac and Manjara Dairy are never quoted from the rate card. Their
prices come from Finance under their annexes.

4.3. Passive shipper hire is quoted only for consignments that start at Nagpur,
because the shippers are at Nagpur. A shipper cannot be quoted on a Guwahati or
Coimbatore dispatch unless the account manager has arranged for the consignment
to go through Nagpur.

4.4. The Guwahati monsoon handling line is quoted only on Guwahati loads in its
months. It is not added to Coimbatore or Nagpur loads.

4.5. The diesel surcharge is quoted as a rule, not as a figure: the agent writes
the rule from the rate card and lets the invoice apply it on the day of travel.

4.6. Agents do not discount. Any price below the rate card is an account
manager's call, confirmed in writing by Finance.

## 7. Gel packs and shipper consumables

7.1. Stores buys gel packs and holds them unconditioned. Conditioning happens in
the QA room, not in Stores.

7.2. Stores keeps at least 44 unconditioned blue-cap packs at Nagpur, enough to
remake two shippers completely.

7.3. Packs retired by QA, for cycle count or for damage, are sent to the
supplier for disposal and recorded as written off. Stores does not throw them in
general waste, because the gel is not general waste.

7.4. White-cap packs are held on a separate shelf, labelled FROZEN GOODS ONLY.

7.5. Spare shipper lids, straps and liners are held by Stores and issued to QA
against a signature. A damaged shipper body is not repaired in Stores.

## 5. Taking a booking

5.1. A booking needs the product class, the quantity in the unit the rate card
uses, the pickup and delivery points, the earliest and latest delivery time, and
the name of the person who will receive.

5.2. The agent checks that the booked vehicle can carry the product class. RF-120
is frozen only; RF-119 takes pharma only with a passive shipper; RF-118 takes
pharma and dairy but never frozen.

5.3. The agent books the dock through Dockwise for Nagpur, Guwahati and
Coimbatore alike. A phone slot at Guwahati is confirmed in Dockwise the next
working day.

5.4. Pharma critical bookings that would need a night segment are passed to
Fleet Control before they are confirmed to the customer, because a night pharma
run needs two named drivers.

5.5. A booking the customer changes after 15:00 the day before is treated as a
new booking.

## 3. Receiving goods

3.1. Goods are received against the purchase order and the delivery note, and
counted before the delivery note is signed. A short delivery is written as short
on the delivery note in front of the supplier's driver.

3.2. Temperature-sensitive consumables, such as conditioned gel packs, are not
received by Stores. They go directly to the QA room.

3.3. Calibrated instruments are received by Stores and passed unopened to the QA
bench on the same day. Stores does not open an instrument box to check it.

3.4. Damaged goods are photographed, set aside and reported to Finance before the
supplier's driver leaves, where that is possible.

# Customer Service Handbook

For customer service agents and account managers at Pune HQ and at the three
DCs. It says how customer service works with customers and with the rest of
Quillfern. It sets no temperature limit, no notification window and no price;
those are in the SOP, the customer notification matrix and the rate card, and an
agent opens those documents rather than quoting this handbook.

## 5. Equipment that has to prove itself

5.1. Every piece of equipment that touches product temperature is qualified before use: the two walk-in chambers, the CRT air-conditioning, the generator and its changeover, and the alarm panel. Qualification means a written test, run by people who did not install the equipment, against acceptance criteria written before the test began.

5.2. The walk-ins are requalified on a fixed cycle, and the cycle was shortened after the compressor failure of November 2025, when WIC-2 ran for nine days on a hired compressor whose behaviour nobody had measured. A full temperature study of each chamber is now repeated every 12 months, and also within 30 days after any compressor, evaporator or door is replaced. The study follows the company mapping method, and the result goes to the RP, who decides whether the chamber may keep holding stock.

5.3. The generator is load-tested on the first Monday of each month by pulling the incoming supply. The changeover must complete before any chamber logger records a rise of more than 1 C, and the technician writes the time it took in his log.

5.4. The alarm panel is tested every Friday. A panel that fails its test is taken out of service and the shift QA officer reads every logger by hand each hour until it is repaired.

5.5. Equipment that fails any test carries a yellow card until it passes again, and the RP is told the same shift. A yellow-carded chamber may keep stock only on the RP's written decision.

## 13. Invoices

13.1. Partners invoice against the work order number, one invoice per work order, with the signed work order and, for Category A, the gas record attached.

13.2. Accounts payable checks each invoice against the work order and the agreed rates. An invoice is accepted when it matches; one that does not is returned within five working days with the reason.

13.3. An accepted invoice is paid within 45 days of acceptance. Partners registered as micro or small enterprises are paid within the period the law requires for them, if that is shorter.

13.4. Payment is made only to the bank account on the partner's file. A request to change the account is confirmed by phone with a known contact at the partner before anything is changed.

13.5. No advance payment is made to any partner without the Finance head's approval.

## 18. Changes to this standard

18.1. Revision 1 (2025) was a one-page checklist used during the 2025 site openings. Revision 2 (February 2026) replaced it with this standard, raised the papers required of Category A partners and set the induction card's validity across sites.

18.2. Procurement reviews this standard every January with QA and the engineering pool.

18.3. Partners are sent a short note of every change, and their agreements are updated at the next renewal.

## 5. Seeing them at home

5.1. Category A partners are visited at their own premises before approval by someone from Procurement and someone from the engineering pool. The visit looks at the workshop, the tools, the stock of spares, the gas recovery equipment, the training records and the way the firm logs its jobs.

5.2. The visit report scores the firm against a written checklist, and a firm that fails any safety item on the checklist is not approved until it has put it right and been visited again.

5.3. Category B partners are visited only where the engineering pool asks. Category C partners are not visited.

5.4. The visit is unannounced in its timing but agreed in principle: the firm knows a visit will come within a month and agrees to admit the visitors on any working day.

## 13. What it costs and when it pays

13.1. The board approved capital spending of Rs. 46 crore for the region: Rs. 31 crore for the DC's fit-out, racking, refrigeration and power, Rs. 6 crore for the satellite, and Rs. 9 crore for the owned fleet.

13.2. Running costs in the first year are budgeted at Rs. 2.1 crore a month at full volume, of which people are about a third and power and fuel another third.

13.3. The region is planned to cover its running costs in its ninth month and to pay back its capital in the twenty-sixth month after first receipt, on contracted volumes only. Any new contract shortens the payback; no forecast is counted until it is signed.

13.4. The region head reports actual against plan to Finance monthly and to the board quarterly.

13.5. Spending above the approved figure needs board approval, however small the overrun.

## 16. Gifts and conflicts

16.1. Nobody at Quillfern accepts a gift, a meal, travel or entertainment from a partner or a firm proposing to become one, beyond token items worth less than Rs. 1,000 in all in a year, such as a diary or a box of sweets at Diwali.

16.2. Anything above that is declined, or, where declining would cause offence, handed to HR and recorded.

16.3. A member of staff with a family or financial interest in a partner declares it to Procurement and takes no part in that partner's approval, scoring or work orders.

16.4. Partners are told these rules when they are approved, and asked to tell Procurement if anyone at Quillfern asks them for anything.

## 8. Power

8.1. The DC has a sanctioned grid load of 1.5 MVA from the state distribution company, on an industrial feeder with its own substation inside the estate.

8.2. Two 750 kVA diesel generator sets stand on a plinth outside the plant room. Either set alone can carry the frozen block, the pharma room and the controls. Both together carry the whole site.

8.3. A rooftop solar plant of 420 kWp feeds the site's own load. It reduces the bill; it is not counted on in an outage.

8.4. The satellite runs on a 250 kVA grid supply and one 320 kVA generator set.

8.5. Changeover is tested monthly at both sites by pulling the incoming supply, and the result is written in the engineering log.

# Quillfern Cold Chain Glossary

Plain meanings for expressions used on site. Short forms are defined in the document that uses them, never here, so an expression below appears in its long form only.

back-to-cold — the moment a staged pallet crosses back over the cold-room threshold; staging time stops here.
chlorine contact time — the minutes a sanitising solution must stay wet on a reefer floor before rinsing; wiping it dry early starts the count again.
dead zone — a stretch of road where the telematics unit cannot report; the USB logger covers it and the gap is recorded as missing, never filled in.
door open minutes — the total minutes a cold-room or reefer door stood open in one shift, summed from the door sensor; a measure of load, not a fault.
holding lane B — the covered waiting lane at Nagpur for pharma and frozen vehicles that miss their dock time; nothing is unloaded there.
mean kinetic temperature — the single steady temperature that would give stock the same total heat stress as the uneven record it actually saw; stability letters are written against it, not against the average.
pre-cool hold time — the minutes an empty reefer body is held at loading temperature, doors shut, before the first pallet goes in.
probe grid — the layout of loggers used when a room is mapped; each position is named by rack, bay and height, such as A1-high.
relief point — a named fuel plaza or rest area on a qualified route where a relief driver or a mobile service van can meet the vehicle.
seal watch — time a driver spends guarding a sealed vehicle; it is duty time and never counts as rest.
shipper conditioning time — the hours a passive shipper's gel packs must sit at their set temperature before the shipper may leave with stock.
stability budget remaining — the minutes above the high limit that a customer's stability letter still allows for one lot, once every earlier excursion on that lot is subtracted.
warm pallet — night-shift name for a pallet whose logger has alarmed but whose excursion QA has not yet confirmed; it is handled as quarantine stock until QA decides.
white tag — the RELEASED tag fixed beside a red hold tag when QA lets stock out of quarantine; the red tag stays on.

## 2. Solution and contact

2.1. The floor, walls to 1 metre, door gaskets and drain channel are wetted with chlorine solution at 200 ppm, mixed fresh for each body.

2.2. The Chlorine Contact Time (CCT) is 10 minutes: the solution stays wet on the surface for that long before rinsing. Wiping the surface dry sooner restarts the count.

2.3. Rinse with potable water, then dry with the doors open and the drain plug out.

## 2. The micro-hub

2.1. The Kothrud micro-hub is a ground-floor unit off Paud Road with a covered
loading lane for two-wheelers and a packing room behind the shutter.

2.2. Stock at Kothrud sits in MCR-4, taken on long hire from the engineering pool. The hub staff do not service it; the engineering pool's own people do,
on their own calendar.

2.3. The packing room holds the packing bench, the carrier rack and PF-K1, the
fridge in which carrier packs are conditioned before use. PF-K1 is not used to
store insulin, even for an hour.

2.4. The hub is open from 06:30 to 22:00 every day. It is staffed by a hub lead
and two packers on each of two shifts.

2.5. Nirmaya's pharmacist visits the hub every working morning to check stock
received from Nirmaya's distributor and to collect anything held for her.

2.6. The hub lead keeps the keys to the store, the packing room and the red
box. Keys are handed over at the shift change against a signature in the key
book.

## 8. Weather and the road

8.1. Riders do not ride in a red weather warning. The hub lead watches the
warnings and stops runs before they start.

8.2. In the monsoon every carrier wears its rain cover, and riders carry a
spare cover in the under-seat box.

8.3. In April and May the midday heat is hard on riders and on carriers. Runs
are planned so that no carrier is in the sun at a long stop, and riders carry
drinking water.

8.4. Riders keep to the speed limits of the roads they ride on and never ride
on a footpath to reach a door.

8.5. A road closure or a rally that blocks a route is reported to the hub, and
the hub lead re-plans the run; the rider does not find a way round on his own.

# Reefer Body Washdown and Sanitation Procedure

## 1. When a washdown is required

1.1. After any dairy spill in the body, before the next load.

1.2. Before a chilled body carries pharma critical stock after any food load.

1.3. Every 14 days for a body on dairy rotation, whether or not anything spilled.

1.4. After any load rejected by a customer for odour.

## 5. Booking a slot

5.1. Nirmaya's care desk books each order into a two-hour slot between 07:00 and
21:00, through the programme portal. The booking names the patient, the address,
the slot and the products.

5.2. The patient receives an SMS with the slot and a one-time code the evening
before, and a second SMS when the rider leaves the hub.

5.3. At the door the rider asks for the OTP. The patient reads out the four-figure code sent by SMS; without it nothing is handed over.

5.4. A patient who has lost the SMS is asked to call the Nirmaya care desk, which
can resend the code. The rider does not accept a name, a photograph or a
neighbour's word instead.

5.5. Slots that the hub cannot meet are moved by the hub lead, never by the
rider, and the patient is called before the original slot begins.

5.6. Nirmaya may book a same-day slot only before 13:00. Same-day bookings after
13:00 go into the next morning.

## 11. Complaints from the person at home

11.1. A patient who complains to a rider is given the Nirmaya care-desk number.
The rider writes down what was said and tells the hub lead before the end of the
shift.

11.2. Complaints that reach Quillfern directly are passed to Nirmaya's care desk
the same day, with the rider's note and the run sheet.

11.3. A complaint about a rider's behaviour or riding goes to the hub lead and
to HR. The rider is told what the complaint says and is asked for his account
before anything is decided.

11.4. Quillfern does not reply to a patient in writing. Written replies come
from Nirmaya.

## 3. Swab check

3.1. Three swabs: floor front, floor rear, door gasket.

3.2. Each must read 150 or below on the handheld luminometer. One failed swab means the whole washdown is repeated, not just the failed spot.

# Pharma Store Quality Manual, West Zone

## 1. Purpose and reach

1.1. The store at Changodar, on the south-west edge of Ahmedabad, is the first Quillfern building that holds medicines and nothing else. It opened in September 2025 in a leased shed inside a pharmaceutical estate off the Sarkhej–Bavla highway. From its first week its customers — two vaccine makers, a biologics firm and three hospital groups in Gujarat — asked for a written quality system they could audit against. This manual is that system. It says how the store keeps product fit for the patient, how it proves that it did so, and who answers when it did not.

1.2. It is written for the people who work in the building: receiving clerks, pickers, dispatch staff, the shift QA officers, the engineering technician and the store manager. It is also written for auditors, who will read it more carefully than anyone on the floor and who should be able to find, somewhere in it, the reason for every record the store keeps.

1.3. Where this manual and a company-wide procedure disagree about a temperature limit, a notification window or a quarantine rule, the company procedure applies and this manual is corrected at its next revision. The manual sets no temperature limit of its own; it says how those limits are kept in this building, by these people.

1.4. Revision 3 is in force from 11/05/2026. The summaries written while the store was being fitted out are withdrawn and kept only as history. Earlier revisions of this manual are withdrawn from the shared drive on the day a new one is issued.

## 4. The calendar

4.1. Civil works at Atchutapuram finished in June 2026. Racking, refrigeration and the electrical fit-out run through the monsoon, with commissioning in October and qualification of the rooms in November.

4.2. The DC receives its first customer stock on 1 December 2026. The date is fixed by Godavari Aqua's contract and it will not move later without the customer's written agreement. Earlier receipts are refused, however much space is ready, because the rooms will not yet have finished qualification.

4.3. The satellite at Bhubaneswar starts cross-dock work on 1 February 2027, eight weeks after the DC, so that the trunk run can be proven with the DC already working.

4.4. Full volume is planned for the end of the first quarter of 2027. From then until the end of 2028, growth is planned in steps tied to signed contracts, not to forecasts.

4.5. Each milestone has a named owner on the project board kept by the region head, and the board is reviewed every Monday.

## 3. Getting a vehicle in and out

3.1. Reefers use the south gate. The east gate is for dry grocery only unless
the DC manager approves an emergency move, as the old wiki page also said.

3.2. School traffic on Temple Street blocks the turn into the south gate between
07:45 and 08:30. Drivers are told on booking to arrive either before 07:30 or
after 08:40. A reefer is never queued across Temple Street; if the apron is
full, the driver goes round the block and comes back.

3.3. Security holds each vehicle outside the south gate until the previous one
has cleared the apron. The apron takes one reefer and one van at a time, no
more, because a reversing reefer cannot see a second one parked behind it.

3.4. Bookings are made in Dockwise, which Coimbatore joined on 1 February 2026.
The grace table and the cancellation rule are the company rule, not a local
one, and are not repeated here.

3.5. Frozen loads are placed before lunch. After about 13:00 the afternoon sun
lies across the outer apron, drivers open their doors to check paperwork, and
the frozen body loses cold it cannot spare.

3.6. Reversing on the apron after dark needs a spotter with a torch, whatever
the vehicle's camera shows. The apron lights are on a timer that the landlord
controls, and they have twice failed to come on in the monsoon.

## 13. What it costs and when it pays

13.1. The board approved capital spending of Rs. 46 crore for the region: Rs. 31 crore for the DC's fit-out, racking, refrigeration and power, Rs. 6 crore for the satellite, and Rs. 9 crore for the owned fleet.

13.2. Running costs in the first year are budgeted at Rs. 2.1 crore a month at full volume, of which people are about a third and power and fuel another third.

13.3. The region is planned to cover its running costs in its ninth month and to pay back its capital in the twenty-sixth month after first receipt, on contracted volumes only. Any new contract shortens the payback; no forecast is counted until it is signed.

13.4. The region head reports actual against plan to Finance monthly and to the board quarterly.

13.5. Spending above the approved figure needs board approval, however small the overrun.

## 6. What stays with us

6.1. Every claim under TPC carries a deductible: a part of each loss that Quillfern bears itself before the insurer pays anything. For 2026–27 the deductible is Rs. 40,000 per consignment. On a loss of Rs. 30,000 the insurer pays nothing; on a loss of Rs. 1,00,000 it pays Rs. 60,000.

6.2. A consignment is one dispatch note. Three pallets on one note make one consignment and carry one deductible. Three notes on one vehicle make three consignments, and each note's loss carries its own deductible.

6.3. Finance books the deductible to the cost centre of the site where the loss happened, or the fleet cost centre where the loss happened on the road. Sites are told their deductible total every quarter.

6.4. Losses below the deductible are still intimated and still recorded. The insurer prices next year's cover on the whole loss record, not only on what it paid, and a record full of gaps is priced as if the gaps were bad news.

6.5. Customers are never told the deductible figure. It is a term of our cover, not of their contract, and quoting it invites an argument about who should bear it.

## 2. The cover in one page

2.1. The policy number is TPC/2026/0417 and the policy year runs from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027. Renewal is negotiated by the claims desk with the broker each February.

2.2. The cover applies to goods in transit by road under a Quillfern dispatch note, in owned vehicles and in hired vehicles alike. It covers the goods from the moment loading begins at the origin dock until unloading ends at the destination. It does not cover goods sitting in a building, which are insured under the property policy, and it does not cover air or sea legs booked by the customer.

2.3. Every dispatch is declared to the broker in a monthly return by the 10th of the following month. The return is generated from the dispatch system by the claims desk and checked by Finance. An undeclared dispatch is not automatically uninsured, but the insurer may ask why it was missed, and a pattern of misses can void the cover.

2.4. The premium is charged on the declared value at 0.11 per cent, adjusted at the year end. The most the insurer will pay across all claims in one policy year is Rs. 9 crore. When claims paid pass Rs. 6 crore the broker tells the claims desk, and the desk tells the Finance head the same day.

2.5. Goods are valued at the value written on the dispatch note or the value in the customer's schedule held by Finance, whichever is lower. A value written in a customer's e-mail after a loss is recorded, but it is not the basis of the claim.

## 9. Pay

9.1. Riders are paid a monthly wage for their shifts, with a small per-drop
addition. The addition is the same for every drop and is not tied to time.

9.2. There is no payment for early arrival and no penalty for a drop that comes
back because the patient was out.

9.3. Fuel for the two-wheelers is paid by Quillfern through a fuel card. Riders
do not pay for fuel from their own money.

9.4. Overtime is paid at the company rate and approved by the hub lead before
the shift is extended, not afterwards.

## 16. Tolls and road charges

16.1. Every owned reefer carries an electronic toll tag registered to Quillfern.
The tag balance is topped up by Fleet Control; drivers never pay a toll in cash
unless the tag reader at the plaza has failed.

16.2. A cash toll is paid only against a printed receipt, which goes into the
trip bag. A handwritten receipt is accepted only when the plaza staff sign and
stamp it.

16.3. A tag that shows a low balance at a plaza is reported to Fleet Control
while parked, and Fleet Control tops it up before the next plaza.

16.4. Hired trucks use their own tags. Quillfern does not refund a hired truck's
tolls unless the purchase order says so.

16.5. Road charges at state borders and permit fees are paid by Fleet Control in
advance for owned reefers. A driver asked for money at a border that was not on
the dispatch note calls Fleet Control before paying anything.

## 14. Changes to this manual

14.1. Revision 1 (August 2025) started the programme with IB-4 carriers. Revision
2 (April 2026) moved the programme to IB-6 carriers and changed the turn-back
rule to match.

14.2. The programme lead reviews this manual every six months with Nirmaya.

14.3. Riders and hub staff send suggested changes to the hub lead at any time.

## 1. What this manual covers

1.1. The manual covers owned reefers, hired reefers, support vans and escort
cars moving under a Quillfern dispatch note, from the moment a vehicle is taken
over at a DC until it is handed back with its paperwork.

1.2. It does not cover warehouse work inside the cold rooms, customer contracts,
or pricing. A driver who is asked a price by a customer refers the customer to
customer service.

1.3. Revision 3 of July 2026 added section 9 on passive shippers in transit and
moved the police-check rules into section 7.

1.4. Where the manual and the Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy seem to
differ, the policy applies. Where the manual and the SOP seem to differ on
anything about temperature, the SOP applies.

1.5. Copies of the manual are kept at the Fleet Control desk in Nagpur, in the
gate cabin at each DC and in the driver rest room at Nagpur. Drivers are not
expected to carry it; the cab card carries what a driver needs on the road.

## 1. What the programme does

1.1. Nirmaya Healthcare runs a home-care service for people with diabetes who
find it hard to collect insulin from a pharmacy. Quillfern holds Nirmaya's
insulin stock in Pune and takes each patient's order to the door on the day and
in the slot the patient booked.

1.2. The programme started on 1 August 2025 with nine riders and about 300 drops
a week. By April 2026 it had 26 riders and about 1,100 drops a week across Pune
and Pimpri-Chinchwad.

1.3. Only insulin pens, cartridges and vials are carried. Vaccines and other
cold medicines are not carried unless Nirmaya adds them by a written change
signed by both sides, and no such change has been signed.

1.4. Quillfern does not advise patients on their medicine. A patient who asks a
rider how much to take, or whether a pen is the right one, is given the Nirmaya
care-desk number printed on the delivery slip.

1.5. Nirmaya owns the stock and the patient relationship. Quillfern owns the
cold chain from the hub to the door, and is answerable for it.

## Half one: red sleeves

The red sleeve is the packet clipped to an excursion file or a pharma truck
file. What it must contain is fixed by clause 4.2 of
[the Temperature Excursion Response SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md); this
project buys the packets and does not change the contents list.

The trigger was operational, not a policy gap. Stores had been promising vendor
plastic sleeves "next week" since April 2026, and the Nagpur night team recorded
a second short packet on 19 June 2026, writing RED SLEEVE MISSING on a printout
for a BharatVac return — see
[the night shift handover log](04-night-shift-handover-log.txt). The same log
records hired trucks arriving without sleeves in October 2025 and staff making
red tags out of old labels.

Ordered: 60 packets at Rs. 1,180 each, split 30 Nagpur, 15 Guwahati,
15 Coimbatore. Each packet is made up with a spare calibrated logger before it
leaves QA, because a sleeve without a logger is the failure this project is
meant to end.

## 5. Red sleeve packets

5.1. Stores holds red sleeve packets empty. QA makes each packet up, including a
spare logger checked at the bench, before it is issued.

5.2. A made-up packet comes back to Stores from QA sealed with a tamper label.
Stores does not open it.

5.3. Stores issues made-up packets to DCs and to reefer cab lockers against a
signature. A packet returned unused and unopened goes back on the shelf; a
packet returned opened goes to QA to be made up again.

5.4. Stores keeps at least ten made-up packets at Nagpur at all times. When the
stock falls to ten, Stores tells QA in writing.

5.5. Packets ordered under the red sleeve project are recorded against that
project's budget line, not against the Stores consumables line.

# PROJ-124: Red sleeve replenishment and passive shipper pilot

**PROJ-124** is open. It has two halves that share a sponsor and a budget line
but nothing else: getting physical red sleeve packets back into every DC, and
piloting validated passive shippers at Nagpur. It is not
[PROJ-123](19-project-PROJ-123-dockwise-rollout.md), which was a dock calendar
project and is closed.

## 4. Immediate containment

4.1. Stop movement of the affected pallet, tote, crate, reefer body, or room bay.
Do not load additional customer stock into the affected compartment.

4.2. Attach a red sleeve to the stock or truck file. The red sleeve contains the
customer intimation form, red hold tags, seal tape, and one spare calibrated
logger. If there is no physical sleeve, print form QCL-F-09 and write RED
SLEEVE MISSING at the top.

4.3. Move warehouse stock to quarantine bay Q-3 at Nagpur, Q-G2 at Guwahati, or
Q-C1 at Coimbatore. Truck stock must remain sealed unless QA instructs unloading
for product safety.

4.4. Photograph the sensor display, seal number, dock clock, and pallet labels.
The first four photographs must be uploaded before anyone debates stock
disposition. Do not wait for the manager to arrive.

4.5. Do not warm, chill, re-ice, ventilate, or hide the probe in order to make a
display look normal. Corrective measures may protect product, but the record
must continue to show the product environment honestly.

4.6. If a reefer unit is unstable on the road, the driver shall stop at a lit
fuel plaza or toll rest area, call Fleet Control, and keep the engine running
unless there is a fire, police order, or personal safety threat.

## Milestones

## 20. Transfers between sites

20.1. Stock sent from Nagpur to Guwahati or Coimbatore travels with a Stores
transfer note on QCL-F-45, listing every item and quantity. The receiving cage
counts the parcel on arrival and signs the note.

20.2. A short or damaged transfer is written on the note and photographed before
the parcel is signed for. The courier is told the same day.

20.3. Numbered stock and made-up red sleeve packets travel in sealed courier
bags. The bag number is written on the transfer note.

20.4. Items are never transferred between sites in a driver's cab, even when a
vehicle happens to be going that way, unless the item is on the dispatch note.

20.5. The signed transfer notes come back to Nagpur by scan the same day and by
post at the month end.

## Out of scope

PROJ-124 does not change any notification timing, any excursion duration or any
dock grace period. It does not buy shippers for Guwahati or Coimbatore; those
sites continue to refuse pharma staging beyond the SOP limit until a later
project is approved.

## 23. Contacts

23.1. The Nagpur store phone is on the Operations extension list. Out of hours,
the night shift lead holds the emergency cupboard key, as in section 2.

23.2. Questions about whether an item is fit to use go to QA. Questions about
whether an item may be bought go to Finance. Stores answers questions about
where an item is and how many are left.

## 2. The Stores team and hours

2.1. The Nagpur store is run by Nalini Patil with two storekeepers on the day
shift. It is open from 07:00 to 19:00, Monday to Saturday.

2.2. At night, the night shift lead holds the key to the emergency cupboard,
which carries red sleeve packets, seal books and protective equipment only.
Anything taken from it at night is written on the cupboard sheet and signed for
properly the next morning.

2.3. The Guwahati cage is looked after by the shift lead named by Riniki Bora.
The Coimbatore cage is looked after by the morning shift lead.

2.4. Stores is not a place to wait, eat or charge a phone. Drivers collecting
seal books or sleeves wait at the counter.

# Stores and Consumables Standard

How Stores receives, holds and issues the consumables that cold-chain work runs
on: seals, red sleeve packets, spare loggers, gel packs, dry ice, protective
equipment and forms. It covers the main store at Nagpur and the smaller stores
cages at Guwahati and Coimbatore. It does not say how any of these items is used
on the job; the documents that govern their use do that.
