## 3. Receiving goods

3.1. Goods are received against the purchase order and the delivery note, and
counted before the delivery note is signed. A short delivery is written as short
on the delivery note in front of the supplier's driver.

3.2. Temperature-sensitive consumables, such as conditioned gel packs, are not
received by Stores. They go directly to the QA room.

3.3. Calibrated instruments are received by Stores and passed unopened to the QA
bench on the same day. Stores does not open an instrument box to check it.

3.4. Damaged goods are photographed, set aside and reported to Finance before the
supplier's driver leaves, where that is possible.

## 2. The Stores team and hours

2.1. The Nagpur store is run by Nalini Patil with two storekeepers on the day
shift. It is open from 07:00 to 19:00, Monday to Saturday.

2.2. At night, the night shift lead holds the key to the emergency cupboard,
which carries red sleeve packets, seal books and protective equipment only.
Anything taken from it at night is written on the cupboard sheet and signed for
properly the next morning.

2.3. The Guwahati cage is looked after by the shift lead named by Riniki Bora.
The Coimbatore cage is looked after by the morning shift lead.

2.4. Stores is not a place to wait, eat or charge a phone. Drivers collecting
seal books or sleeves wait at the counter.

## 24. Review of this standard

24.1. Nalini Patil reviews this standard every July with QA and Finance, and
sooner when a new consumable is introduced or a supplier changes.

24.2. A change to how an item is used is made in the document that governs its
use, not here. This standard changes only how Stores receives, holds, issues and
counts the item.

24.3. Each revision is issued with a note of what changed. The storekeepers at
Nagpur and the cage leads at Guwahati and Coimbatore sign that they have read it
within a week.

24.4. The earlier revision is withdrawn from the Stores counter and the shared
drive on the day the new one is issued, so that nobody works from two versions
at the same time.

## 14. Layout and labelling of the store

14.1. The Nagpur store is laid out in four zones: numbered stock in the locked
cage, instruments on the shelf beside the QA hatch, protective equipment on the
open racks, and general consumables at the back.

14.2. Every shelf carries a printed label with the item name, the Stores item
code and the minimum stock. A handwritten label is replaced within a week.

14.3. Heavy items are stored below waist height. Nothing is stored on top of the
cage or on the floor of the walkway.

14.4. The store floor is swept daily and the racks are dusted monthly. Wet items
are never brought into the store; they are dried outside first.

14.5. The Guwahati and Coimbatore cages follow the same labels and item codes as
Nagpur, so that a count sheet from any site reads the same way.

## 4. Frozen bodies

4.1. A frozen body such as RF-120 is never washed with water while the body is below 0 C. It is dry-wiped with food-grade alcohol, and gets a full washdown only when defrosted at service.

4.2. A raw chicken spill in a frozen body is the exception: the body is taken out of service and defrosted for a full washdown within 24 hours.

## 11. Write-off and disposal

11.1. Stores writes off an item only with Finance's approval, recorded on the
write-off sheet.

11.2. Broken instruments are written off after QA has confirmed they cannot be
calibrated. Their serials are struck off the instrument list.

11.3. Damaged seal books are never thrown away. Every seal in them is written
VOID and kept with the stubs until the next audit.

11.4. Protective equipment that is worn out is cut before disposal, so that it
cannot be picked out of the bin and worn again.

## 5. Where and who

5.1. Nagpur: the wash bay beside the generator room. Guwahati: the contract garage. Coimbatore: the wash pad inside the south gate.

5.2. The shift lead signs the wash register QCL-F-40. The driver may do the washdown but may not sign it.

## 7. People at the gate

7.1. A technician who will enter a pharma zone, a cold room holding pharma stock or a QA area must have a police verification certificate obtained through the local police station. The partner obtains it and sends us a copy before the technician's first visit.

7.2. The certificate must be renewed every three years. A technician whose certificate is more than three years old is refused at the gate, whatever the job, until a renewed certificate arrives.

7.3. Technicians who work only outside product zones need no police verification under this standard, though a site may require it for its own reasons.

7.4. Partners send the name, photograph and mobile number of every technician they may send. The gate is not expected to admit a technician who is not on the partner's list, even if the firm calls ahead.

7.5. Technicians leave their phones in the gate locker before entering a pharma zone unless the job needs a phone and the shift lead agrees.

## 4. Immediate containment

4.1. Stop movement of the affected pallet, tote, crate, reefer body, or room bay.
Do not load additional customer stock into the affected compartment.

4.2. Attach a red sleeve to the stock or truck file. The red sleeve contains the
customer intimation form, red hold tags, seal tape, and one spare calibrated
logger. If there is no physical sleeve, print form QCL-F-09 and write RED
SLEEVE MISSING at the top.

4.3. Move warehouse stock to quarantine bay Q-3 at Nagpur, Q-G2 at Guwahati, or
Q-C1 at Coimbatore. Truck stock must remain sealed unless QA instructs unloading
for product safety.

4.4. Photograph the sensor display, seal number, dock clock, and pallet labels.
The first four photographs must be uploaded before anyone debates stock
disposition. Do not wait for the manager to arrive.

4.5. Do not warm, chill, re-ice, ventilate, or hide the probe in order to make a
display look normal. Corrective measures may protect product, but the record
must continue to show the product environment honestly.

4.6. If a reefer unit is unstable on the road, the driver shall stop at a lit
fuel plaza or toll rest area, call Fleet Control, and keep the engine running
unless there is a fire, police order, or personal safety threat.

## 3. Exceptions

3.1. If weather, police stoppage, road closure, civil disturbance, vehicle
breakdown, medical emergency, or a safety threat would cause a driver to exceed
a limit, the driver must stop at the nearest lit fuel plaza, toll rest area,
police post, customer secure yard, or Quillfern DC.

3.2. Fleet Control shall log the exception under code SANDHU-EXC with the time,
place, reason, stock type, driver statement, and revised plan. The exception is
not closed until a rest plan is recorded.

3.3. A cold-chain emergency is not by itself a driving-hours exception. The
correct response is to secure the vehicle, protect the product, and arrange a
replacement driver, mobile service, or customer-approved transfer.

3.4. Managers shall not instruct a driver to "push through", "make up time", or
"just reach the next DC" after the legal or Quillfern limit is reached. Such an
instruction is misconduct even when no crash occurs.

## 5. Notifications

5.1. Pharma critical stock means vaccines, insulin, and any medicine named by a
customer as patient critical. The customer must be notified within 2 hours of a
confirmed pharma critical excursion.

5.2. Dairy customers must be notified by the next scheduled customer service
check-in unless spoilage is visible, odour is present, or the temperature is
above +8.0 C. In those cases customer service must notify within 4 hours.

5.3. Frozen-food restaurant chains must receive an exception notice by the end of
the business day when the excursion is confirmed. If the vehicle is still on the
road, Fleet Control must also call the receiving kitchen.

5.4. Internal escalation for all pharma critical events goes to Compliance-Red,
the DC manager, Fleet Control if a truck is involved, and Finance if stock is
likely to be destroyed.

5.5. Customer notice must say "temperature excursion under investigation" until
QA approves a final wording. Staff must not promise release, replacement credit,
or insurance recovery in the first notice.

## 2. Three kinds of partner

2.1. Category A partners work on temperature-critical plant: refrigeration, the controllers and alarms on cold rooms, the generators and changeover gear that keep them running, and the reefer units on vehicles.

2.2. Category B partners work on the building and its fixed equipment but not on temperature-critical plant: dock doors and levellers, electrical work outside the plant room, roofing, fire equipment, pest control.

2.3. Category C partners neither touch plant nor enter product zones: office cleaning, canteen, landscaping, office IT.

2.4. The category decides how much checking a firm needs. A firm doing work in two categories is approved in the higher one.

2.5. Procurement assigns the category when the firm is proposed. The site manager or the engineering pool may ask for a firm to be moved to a higher category; nobody may move one lower without Procurement and QA agreeing.

## 12. Passing work on

12.1. A partner may not pass any part of a Quillfern job to another firm without Procurement's written consent before the work is done. A firm that subcontracts without consent is suspended.

12.2. Consent is given only where the other firm meets the same category's requirements in this standard, including the papers in section 4 and police verification where section 7 requires it.

12.3. Specialist work that the partner cannot do itself — crane hire, scaffolding, a manufacturer's own warranty technician — may be brought in with the shift lead's agreement on the day, but the partner remains responsible for it.

12.4. Agency labour sent in place of the partner's own technicians counts as subcontracting.

## 8. Records

8.1. Dispatch notes, Tessaline or Kalpa trip reports, driver call logs, exception
forms, and gate registers together form the driving-hours record.

8.2. Records must be kept for three years. Where a pharma critical excursion,
crash, insurance claim, or police matter is involved, the record must be kept
for seven years.

8.3. Fleet and HR jointly review this policy every April. Emergency amendments
may be issued by the Fleet head, but HR must publish them within five working
days.

## Mock recall

## Mock recall

A mock recall is run once a year, in November, on a batch the QA lead picks.
Every unit of the chosen batch must be traced, on the shelf, on a vehicle or at
a consignee, within 8 hours of the exercise starting. The result goes to the
batch owner.

## 11. After the stock has left

11.1. Responsibility for a batch does not end at the dispatch bay. The store must be able to find every unit it has handled, and it must deal properly with what comes back.

11.2. Twice a year, in March and September, the store runs a mock recall on a batch chosen by the RP without warning. The exercise starts when she names the batch to the shift QA officer. Every unit of the chosen batch must be found and named — on a shelf, on a vehicle or at a consignee — inside four hours of the exercise starting. The result, with the time taken and any unit that could not be found, goes to the customer who owns the batch.

11.3. Hospitals and distributors send product back for many reasons — over-ordering, a ward closing, a wrong delivery — and none of those reasons makes it fit to be resold. Nothing returned goes back into saleable stock unless it comes back within 72 hours of delivery, with an unbroken logger record from our hands to the consignee's and back, and the Responsible Person signs the release; everything else is destroyed. Returned product waits in the quarantine cage while the decision is made.

11.4. A real recall, as opposed to a practice one, is run by the customer. The store's part is to stop dispatch of the batch at once, list every unit it holds and every unit it has sent, and hold any returned units in quarantine until the customer instructs.

11.5. Complaints from hospitals about a product's quality are passed to the customer the same day. The store does not reply to the complaint itself, and does not offer an opinion on it.

# Vadodara bonded store card: mock recall, returned goods back to stock, batch record retention

Pinned at the Vadodara QA desk. This card covers three things: the mock recall,
when returned goods may go back to stock, and how long batch records are kept.

## 2. What the store promises

2.1. The store promises its customers four things: that a product is held inside its labelled conditions from the moment it crosses the dock until the moment it leaves; that every unit can be traced; that anything which goes wrong is written down honestly, even when it is embarrassing; and that nothing doubtful reaches a patient because a delivery was due.

2.2. Those promises are not slogans for the canteen wall. Each has a record behind it, and the sections below say which. A promise without a record is treated in an audit as a promise not kept.

2.3. The store manager, Bhavesh Rana, owns the operation. The site QA lead, Hemal Trivedi, owns this manual and the quality records. The RP, Dr. Nupur Shah, is the pharmacist named on the wholesale licence and the only person who may release stock for supply. The three roles are deliberately kept in different hands, so that the person who has to meet the dispatch plan is never the person who decides whether doubtful stock may go.

2.4. Customers are told these names on the day their account opens, and told again whenever one of them changes. A customer's quality agreement may add obligations to this manual but may not remove any.

## 8. Heavy days on the road

8.1. The insurer's exposure on any single vehicle is capped. The most it will pay for all goods on one vehicle on one trip is Rs. 1.2 crore, however many consignments are on board.

8.2. A full vaccine load easily goes past that figure, and so does a frozen load of premium seafood. Any dispatch whose total declared value on one vehicle is above Rs. 1.2 crore is declared to the broker in writing at least 48 hours before the vehicle leaves. The broker then gets the insurer's agreement to a higher figure for that trip, or tells us to split the load.

8.3. Fleet planners check the declared value of every pharma critical and every high-value frozen load when they build the week's plan, and send the list of trips over the figure to the claims desk on Thursday.

8.4. A trip that goes over the figure without a declaration is still covered up to Rs. 1.2 crore. Anything above that is uninsured, and the site manager who allowed the load explains why in writing.

8.5. Splitting a load costs a second vehicle and a second crew. Planners should prefer splitting to asking for a higher figure only where the second vehicle is already on the road; the broker's higher figure usually costs less than an empty run.

## 14. Layout and labelling of the store

14.1. The Nagpur store is laid out in four zones: numbered stock in the locked
cage, instruments on the shelf beside the QA hatch, protective equipment on the
open racks, and general consumables at the back.

14.2. Every shelf carries a printed label with the item name, the Stores item
code and the minimum stock. A handwritten label is replaced within a week.

14.3. Heavy items are stored below waist height. Nothing is stored on top of the
cage or on the floor of the walkway.

14.4. The store floor is swept daily and the racks are dusted monthly. Wet items
are never brought into the store; they are dried outside first.

14.5. The Guwahati and Coimbatore cages follow the same labels and item codes as
Nagpur, so that a count sheet from any site reads the same way.

## 8. North-east monsoon and the afternoon sun

8.1. Coimbatore's heavy rain comes with the north-east monsoon, from October to
December, not in the June to September months that set the calendar at Nagpur
and Guwahati.

8.2. Rain cover over rear pallets is used at Coimbatore from October to December
whenever it is raining on the apron. The site owns six tarpaulins for this.

8.3. Coimbatore does not bill the customer for rain cover. The monsoon handling
line on the rate card is a Guwahati charge and is not quoted for Coimbatore
loads. Customer service agents who copy the Guwahati line onto a Coimbatore
quotation create a credit note later.

8.4. The hot months are March to May. In those months the afternoon rule in
section 3.5 is enforced strictly, and the wash pad is used before 11:00 so that
washed bodies are not left drying in the midday sun with their doors open.

8.5. The cold block wall sweats in the monsoon. Anything stored against it on
the dry side is moved 30 cm away from the wall from October onwards.

6.4. The two-person figure is lower at Coimbatore than elsewhere because the
path from the shed to the apron crosses the wash pad, which is wet for most of
the day.

6.5. Dry ice never goes into CBE-PHARMA, never into the closed dairy room, and
never into a cab. Unused pellets go back to the chest in the same shift.

## 7. Leaving the building in a hurry

7.1. The Coimbatore cold block runs on packaged refrigeration units on the roof.
There is no ammonia on this site, so the ammonia cards used at Nagpur do not
apply here and must not be pinned up here.

7.2. Coimbatore has one site siren, and it means leave the building. It sounds
for fire, for a gas smell from the canteen cylinders, and for a refrigerant leak
alarm from a roof unit.

7.3. Everyone goes to assembly point CM-1, the coconut grove corner inside the
east gate. Nobody gathers on the south apron: that is where the fire tender
comes in.

7.4. The shift lead counts against the gate register and the Dockwise day list,
and phones the count to the DC manager. Drivers waiting outside the south gate
stay outside and are counted by the guard.

7.5. Nobody goes back into the cold block for stock. Pallets left outside a room
are dealt with afterwards under the SOP.

7.6. The all clear is given in person by the DC manager or, at night, by the
senior guard after the fire service leaves.

## 1. What Stores does

1.1. Stores buys nothing on its own authority. It raises a request against a
purchase order that Finance has approved, receives the goods, holds them, issues
them against a signature and counts them.

1.2. The Nagpur main store keeps the stock for Nagpur and sends stock to
Guwahati and Coimbatore by courier or on a scheduled vehicle. The Guwahati and
Coimbatore cages hold only what their DC uses in about a month.

1.3. Every item issued is signed for by the person who takes it. An item that
leaves Stores without a signature is counted as lost at the next count.

1.4. Stores does not lend. An item taken for a job is either used, returned or
written off, and each of those is recorded.

## 2. The Stores team and hours

2.1. The Nagpur store is run by Nalini Patil with two storekeepers on the day
shift. It is open from 07:00 to 19:00, Monday to Saturday.

2.2. At night, the night shift lead holds the key to the emergency cupboard,
which carries red sleeve packets, seal books and protective equipment only.
Anything taken from it at night is written on the cupboard sheet and signed for
properly the next morning.

2.3. The Guwahati cage is looked after by the shift lead named by Riniki Bora.
The Coimbatore cage is looked after by the morning shift lead.

2.4. Stores is not a place to wait, eat or charge a phone. Drivers collecting
seal books or sleeves wait at the counter.

## 22. Energy and waste in the store

22.1. The store lights are on a timer and go off at 19:30. The storekeeper
closing the store checks that the cage, the flammables cabinet and the emergency
cupboard are locked before the lights go off.

22.2. Packaging from deliveries is flattened and sent to the scrap area on the
day it arrives. The store is not a place to keep empty boxes.

22.3. Used toner cartridges are returned to the toner supplier for recycling.

22.4. Stores reports its waste once a year to the Nagpur DC manager, by type and
weight, for the site's environmental return.

## 3. Gate and apron

3.1. The gate is staffed round the clock. Every vehicle is logged in with its
registration, its seal number, the customer and the time, and logged out the
same way. A vehicle that leaves without being logged out is reported to the site
manager the same shift.

3.2. The apron takes nine vehicles. Brand owners often drop a trailer and take
the tractor away, collecting the empty trailer later; a dropped trailer stands
on the apron with its reefer unit running on the shore-power posts along the
south fence.

3.3. Reefer units are plugged into shore power within 15 minutes of a trailer
being dropped. A driver who leaves a reefer running on diesel on the apron is
asked to plug it in, and the guard notes the time on the gate log.

3.4. Detention on a trailer that a customer has dropped or sent is billed to
that customer, not absorbed by the site. The clock starts at gate-in; nothing is charged for the first three hours, and each started hour after that costs Rs. 900. On the invoice it appears as a wait-time line and is taxed in the same way
as one.

3.5. Until 31 March 2026 four hours were free. The window came down from 1 April
2026, when two apron bays were lost to the enlarged cell behind D3 and every
remaining bay became worth more.

3.6. The guard does not decide detention. The office works it out from the gate
log at the end of each day, and a customer who disputes a line is sent the gate
log entries themselves, not a summary of them.

3.7. Reversing onto D1 and D2 after dark needs a spotter with a torch. The apron
lights run from the site's own supply and stay on when the grid fails.

3.8. Trailers are never parked across the fire lane that runs along the north
fence to the plant room door. The lane is marked in red hatching and is checked
by the guard at every shift change.

## 13. Cabs, bodies and how they look

13.1. A Quillfern cab is kept clean enough that a customer's receiving clerk can
sit in it to sign papers. Food wrappers, bottles and bedding are cleared out at
the end of every duty day.

13.2. Nothing is stuck to the windscreen except the permits the law requires and
the Quillfern asset number. Stickers, pictures and hanging charms that block the
driver's view are removed at the takeover walk-round.

13.3. The outside of the body is washed at least once a week, and after any run
through a construction zone or mud. A body whose company markings cannot be read
is washed before its next customer drop.

13.4. Scratches and dents are reported, not painted over. Fleet Control books
body repairs in batches so that no vehicle is off the road longer than it needs
to be.

13.5. The cab card, the red sleeve and the fire extinguisher each have a fixed
place in the cab. A driver who finds any of them moved puts it back and tells
Fleet Control, because the next driver will look for it in its fixed place in a
hurry.

## 2. The work

2.1. Quillfern collects the customer's frozen products from the Chakan factory,
stores them and delivers them to restaurants, caterers and retailers in Pune
and Mumbai.

2.2. Pune deliveries go out from Quillfern's own stock. Mumbai-bound stock is
cross-docked at Quillfern's Bhiwandi site and goes out on the next morning's
vans.

2.3. Call-off times for Mumbai deliveries are those printed in the site handbook of the cross-dock that ships them.

2.4. Waiting charges on the customer's own vehicles at the cross-dock are billed at the site's published rate less 20 per cent.

2.5. Pallets are exchanged one for one at the cross-dock. Exchange units that arrive unfit on the customer's own vehicles are charged at the site figure, with no discount.

2.6. Quillfern does not sell, promote or price the customer's products and does
not take orders from the customer's buyers directly.

# Consolidated Service Terms, Contract CN-31

The terms on which Quillfern Cold Logistics Pvt. Ltd. stores and delivers frozen
products for Saptagiri Foods Pvt. Ltd., as they stand after the two amendments.
This consolidation is prepared by Finance for the people who run the account. It
replaces nothing; the signed agreement and its amendments remain the legal
record, and where this text and the signed record differ, the signed record
applies.

## 1. Parties and how to read this

1.1. The parties are Quillfern Cold Logistics Pvt. Ltd. ("Quillfern") and
Saptagiri Foods Pvt. Ltd. ("the customer"), a maker of frozen parathas, samosas
and snacks with a factory at Chakan.

1.2. The agreement began on 1 April 2025 and runs until either side ends it under section 10.

1.3. Amendment 1 took effect on 1 October 2025 and changed the payment terms.
Amendment 2 took effect on 1 April 2026 and changed the liability cap. Both are
folded into the text below and listed in section 15.

1.4. Clause numbers here follow this consolidation, not the original agreement.
A clause quoted from the signed record carries its original number.

## 15. Review of this handbook

15.1. The site manager reviews this handbook every June and after any serious
incident, audit finding or change to the building.

15.2. Revision 3 of June 2026 recorded the new apron free window, the larger cell
and the earlier order cut-off, and moved the genset rules into their own
section.

15.3. Suggestions from staff go to the site manager at any time. Each one is
answered, whether or not it is taken up.

15.4. A revised handbook replaces every earlier copy in the office, the guard
cabin and the canteen on the day it is issued.

# Western Frozen Cross-Dock Handbook

How the western frozen cross-dock is run, written for the people who work there
and for anyone from another site who is sent to help in a busy week. The site
moves frozen food from manufacturers' trailers to city delivery vans for Mumbai,
Thane and Navi Mumbai. It is a cross-dock first and a store second: stock is
meant to come in, be checked, be sorted and go out, and the building is sized
for that and nothing more. Company rules on temperature, driving and hygiene
apply here as everywhere; this handbook says how they are carried out in this
building, with these doors, this yard and this traffic.

## 8. Price movement

8.1. Quillfern's charges are those in the schedule of rates signed with the
agreement, as moved under this section.

8.2. Rates move once a year on 1 April, by no more than the change in the wholesale price index over the previous twelve months plus two points.

8.3. Quillfern sends the new rates by 1 March. The customer may ask for the
working behind them and Quillfern will show it.

8.4. Fuel is not part of the rates. A fuel surcharge applies to transport on
Quillfern's standard terms in force on the day of travel.

## 5. Temperatures

5.1. The customer's products are kept at -18 C or colder in storage and in
transit.

5.2. The customer pre-cools each trailer before loading at Chakan and sends the
pre-cool record with the trailer.

5.3. Product that turns up above minus 12 is brought down to temperature at the cross-dock, and that work is invoiced to the customer.

5.4. Quillfern is not liable for product damage caused by temperatures before
handover. Each party may inspect the other's temperature records for its
stock.

## 18. Things left out on purpose

18.1. The satellite does not store medicines and does not unload them. Pharma stock for Odisha customers either travels direct from the DC in a sealed vehicle that passes through the satellite's yard without opening, or is delivered by the DC's own vehicle. No passive shipper, no cross-dock exception and no customer's urgency changes this.

18.2. The region does not handle live seafood, fresh fish on ice or any product that is not packed and labelled.

18.3. The region does not offer customs clearance as a service. The exporter's own agent clears its goods; we provide the space and the supervision of stuffing.

18.4. The DC does not open a retail counter or sell surplus stock locally.

## 2. The work

2.1. Quillfern collects the customer's frozen products from the Chakan factory,
stores them and delivers them to restaurants, caterers and retailers in Pune
and Mumbai.

2.2. Pune deliveries go out from Quillfern's own stock. Mumbai-bound stock is
cross-docked at Quillfern's Bhiwandi site and goes out on the next morning's
vans.

2.3. Call-off times for Mumbai deliveries are those printed in the site handbook of the cross-dock that ships them.

2.4. Waiting charges on the customer's own vehicles at the cross-dock are billed at the site's published rate less 20 per cent.

2.5. Pallets are exchanged one for one at the cross-dock. Exchange units that arrive unfit on the customer's own vehicles are charged at the site figure, with no discount.

2.6. Quillfern does not sell, promote or price the customer's products and does
not take orders from the customer's buyers directly.

## 9. Insulin without spare cold

9.1. Coimbatore holds no passive shippers, no gel packs and no conditioning
cabinet. The passive shipper pilot is at Nagpur only, and it does not extend to
Coimbatore until a later project is approved.

9.2. Because there are no shippers, insulin at Coimbatore is never staged on an
open dock beyond the SOP limit. Insulin moves from CBE-PHARMA straight into a
reefer body that is already at loading temperature, and the reefer waits for
the insulin, never the other way round.

9.3. A customer who asks Coimbatore for a shipper-packed consignment is told
that the site cannot pack one. The account manager may arrange for a
shipper-packed consignment to come from Nagpur.

9.4. Coimbatore does not stock blue-cap or white-cap packs of any kind, and does
not freeze packs in CBE-FROZEN for customers. A customer's own packs returned
with a consignment go back with the customer's return challan.

## 11. Inland from the coast

11.1. The site at Bhubaneswar exists to bring the DC's stock to customers in Odia-speaking markets the next morning, and to collect stock from Kalinga Biologicals and from Odisha food makers for the DC.

11.2. It is a cross-dock. Goods arriving on the nightly trunk run are sorted and loaded onto local vans for delivery the same morning. Goods collected locally wait for the next night's trunk run back to the DC.

11.3. No pallet stays at the satellite for more than 36 hours from arrival. A pallet still there at hour 30 is reported to the DC manager, who decides whether it goes back on the next trunk run or out on a special van.

11.4. Because nothing is stored there, the satellite does not hold a storage licence for medicines, and pharma stock passes through it only in the trunk vehicle without being unloaded (section 18).

11.5. The site's staging hall is mapped like a room, though it is not a store, because stock stands in it during sorting.

## 2. The two sites

2.1. The Visakhapatnam DC stands on a leased plot of 4.2 acres in the Atchutapuram industrial area, south-west of the city, about 18 km by road from the port's outer gate. The building is a new pre-engineered shed with a cold block, a frozen block, a small controlled-room-temperature store, a dispatch canopy and a two-storey office.

2.2. The satellite at Bhubaneswar is a smaller leased unit in the Mancheswar industrial estate. It has two chilled docks, two frozen docks, a staging hall held at +4 C and a site office. It is a cross-dock, not a store.

2.3. The two sites are about 440 km apart by the coastal highway. A nightly trunk run links them.

2.4. The DC is the region's centre: its manager is the senior manager in the region, its QA lead covers both sites, and its engineering team maintains the satellite's plant.

2.5. Both leases run for fifteen years with a right to renew. The landlord at Atchutapuram built the shell to our drawings; the fit-out, racking and refrigeration belong to Quillfern.

## 5. Temperatures

5.1. The customer's products are kept at -18 C or colder in storage and in
transit.

5.2. The customer pre-cools each trailer before loading at Chakan and sends the
pre-cool record with the trailer.

5.3. Product that turns up above minus 12 is brought down to temperature at the cross-dock, and that work is invoiced to the customer.

5.4. Quillfern is not liable for product damage caused by temperatures before
handover. Each party may inspect the other's temperature records for its
stock.

## 4. Product, packing and handover

4.1. The customer packs its products in cartons that carry the batch number and
the best-before date on two faces.

4.2. Loaded pallets stand no higher than 1.8 metres including the wooden base. Taller pallets are restacked at the customer's cost before they are
accepted.

4.3. Each pallet is stretch-wrapped and labelled with the customer's pallet ID
on two faces.

4.4. Handover takes place when the pallet crosses the dock edge at the
receiving site. The receiving shift lead's count is the count.

## 8. Price movement

8.1. Quillfern's charges are those in the schedule of rates signed with the
agreement, as moved under this section.

8.2. Rates move once a year on 1 April, by no more than the change in the wholesale price index over the previous twelve months plus two points.

8.3. Quillfern sends the new rates by 1 March. The customer may ask for the
working behind them and Quillfern will show it.

8.4. Fuel is not part of the rates. A fuel surcharge applies to transport on
Quillfern's standard terms in force on the day of travel.

6.4. The two-person figure is lower at Coimbatore than elsewhere because the
path from the shed to the apron crosses the wash pad, which is wet for most of
the day.

6.5. Dry ice never goes into CBE-PHARMA, never into the closed dairy room, and
never into a cab. Unused pellets go back to the chest in the same shift.

## 7. Goods arriving

7.1. A vehicle arriving at the store is checked before it is opened: the seal number against the paperwork, the condition of the doors and the reefer's display. The driver stays with the vehicle until goods-in has finished with it, and is offered the drivers' room, not the canteen.

7.2. Every inbound vehicle's temperature printout or download is read at the goods-in desk before a single pallet crosses the threshold. Drivers call any missing stretch a "hole" in the printout, and holes are common on loads that come round the Ahmedabad ring road, where some older reefers lose their logger signal. A break of up to ten minutes in the record may be accepted by the goods-in clerk; anything longer goes to the Responsible Person, who decides. A record that is in range throughout but shows the reefer door opening during the journey is also referred to her.

7.3. Pallets are checked against the advance notice by batch and quantity. A batch that does not match the notice is received into quarantine rather than refused at the door, so that the customer's stock is protected while the paperwork is put right.

7.4. Goods-in photographs every pallet label before the stretch wrap is cut. The photographs are filed against the receipt, not kept on the camera.

7.5. Nothing is received between 22:00 and 06:00. A vehicle that arrives at night waits outside the estate gate on its own power, and its record for the waiting hours is read together with the journey.

## 16. Leaving Quillfern

16.1. Leavers hand back every device, battery and charger issued to them by name, and the shift lead signs the asset register to show it was received. HR does not issue the leaving papers until the register is signed.

16.2. Sometimes a person who quits keeps their scanner, by accident or otherwise. Anything not returned within two working days of the last shift is recovered from the final settlement at Rs. 18,500 per K7 and Rs. 6,200 per LP-40. The device is then locked and wiped from Fernguard.

16.3. A device returned after the recovery is made is refunded at the same rate, less any repair cost.

16.4. Agency staff never hold a named device, so nothing is recovered from their agencies; their day credentials simply lapse.

16.5. Trainees who leave the Waluj programme early hand their device back to the trainer the same day.

## 2. The kit

2.1. The K7 is a rugged Android terminal with a built-in barcode reader, a 5-inch screen, a hot-swap battery and a wrist strap. It is rated for drops of 1.8 m onto concrete and for use in rain, but not for long use in a freezer (section 10).

2.2. The LP-40 is a belt-clip thermal printer for pallet and carton labels. It pairs with one K7 over Bluetooth.

2.3. Each K7 sits in a charging cradle when not in use. Cradles are mounted on cradle racks of ten, one rack per shift area, and each rack holds two spare K7s that belong to the rack rather than to a person.

2.4. Every device carries an asset label with its number, and Fernguard knows every device by its serial number. An asset label that is peeling is replaced by the IT desk, not taped over.

2.5. No other phone, tablet or scanner may be used for stock work at these sites. A customer's own scanner brought by an auditor is used only to read, never to transact.

2.6. The fleet at the date of this revision is 118 K7s and 34 LP-40s across the four sites, with the numbers per site held in the asset register. The register, not this policy, is the place to check a count.

## 3. Who answers for what

3.1. The RP answers to the licensing authority as well as to Quillfern. She may stop any dispatch at any hour without giving a reason first; the reason is written up within the shift.

3.2. Shift QA officers work under the RP. One is on duty on each of the two shifts, 06:00 to 14:00 and 14:00 to 22:00. Between 22:00 and 06:00 the store neither receives nor dispatches except under a written plan the RP has approved, and the night is covered by the security contractor and the RP's phone.

3.3. The engineering technician, Irfan Ghanchi, looks after the chambers, the generator, the alarm panel and the loggers. He keeps his own maintenance log. He does not decide whether stock affected by an equipment fault is usable; he reports the fault and the QA officer decides what happens to the stock.

3.4. The store manager decides staffing, slots and vehicles. He may ask QA to hurry; he may not ask QA to agree. Where any two of these people disagree about whether stock may move, it does not move until the RP has decided.

3.5. Each role has a named deputy, listed on the board outside the QA office. A deputy acts with the full authority of the role while the holder is away, and signs in the deputy's own name, never the holder's.

# Changodar pharma store: quality summary for fit-out

Written during the fit-out of the Changodar pharma store so that the first
customers had something to audit against before the quality manual existed.

## 9. Overnight

9.1. Software and app updates are pushed from Fernguard to docked devices only, so that nobody's scanner restarts in the middle of a pick. New software is tested on four devices at the Waluj workshop first.

9.2. The push window is Tuesday night, 01:00 to 03:00, and a K7 that is not in its cradle then is updated the following Tuesday. A device that has missed two windows is called in by the desk.

9.3. Urgent security updates may be pushed outside the window. The desk warns the shift leads first, and the update waits for the device to be docked.

9.4. Nobody updates a K7 by hand, from a memory card or from a cable.

9.5. Sites that work through Tuesday night arrange their docking so that each rack is full for at least an hour inside the window.

## Humidity limit in the CRT area

The CRT area is held at or below 60 per cent RH.

## 6. Who may use one

6.1. A K7 may be used only by a person with a login issued by the IT desk. Logins are personal; a shift lead does not sign in for a picker so the picker can start sooner.

6.2. Contract and agency workers do not get permanent logins. Agency staff on the scanners are some of the busiest users on a peak night, and each one is given a temporary sign-in for the shift at the shift lead's request to the desk. The desk issues them a day credential that stops working twelve hours after it is first used. A new one is issued for each shift worked.

6.3. Personal phones are a separate matter. Many staff would rather scan with their own phone than walk to the rack, and on the pilot some did. No personal phone may run the scanning app or hold a Quillfern login, even for one shift when a K7 has failed; the user takes a spare from the cradle rack or waits.

6.4. Customer staff and auditors may look at a K7's screen with a Quillfern user beside them. They do not operate it.

6.5. Trainees from the Waluj workshop use a K7 only with their trainer's login running, and only for the exercises in their module.

## 5. Apps on the device

5.1. A K7 runs the warehouse picking app, the receiving app, the document viewer, the camera and nothing else. The app list is fixed by Fernguard.

5.2. Users cannot install apps, and a K7 that shows an app not on the list is taken out of use and returned to the IT desk.

5.3. The camera is for evidence: damaged cartons, seal numbers, pallet labels. Photographs taken on a K7 upload to the document system and are deleted from the device after upload.

5.4. The browser is locked to the document system and the company intranet. A user who needs another website uses an office PC.

5.5. Messaging apps are not installed. Shift instructions come through the shift lead, not through the device.

5.6. A request for a new app on the list goes from the site manager to the IT infrastructure lead in writing, with the reason. The app is tested at the Waluj workshop on four devices for a fortnight before it reaches a live site.

## 13. Language and new people

13.1. Coimbatore works in Tamil. Training is given by a trainer in Tamil, with
English slides available but never used instead of a trainer.

13.2. New joiners spend their first week on the morning shift only. They are not
put on the late shift, and never left alone in the cold block, until a shift
lead has signed them off.

13.3. Every new joiner is shown the gate cabin, the security roster and the key
register on the first day. They are told that security will not open anything
for them at night except in an emergency, and that the lockers, the cabinet and
the seal drawer are all separate keys.

13.4. New drivers from hired-truck vendors are shown the south gate routine by
the guard and the Temple Street timing by the shift lead before their first
booking.

13.5. The words used on site follow the company glossary. A new joiner who hears
a word they do not know is expected to ask, on any shift, and nobody at
Coimbatore is to laugh at the question.

## 9. Overnight

9.1. Software and app updates are pushed from Fernguard to docked devices only, so that nobody's scanner restarts in the middle of a pick. New software is tested on four devices at the Waluj workshop first.

9.2. The push window is Tuesday night, 01:00 to 03:00, and a K7 that is not in its cradle then is updated the following Tuesday. A device that has missed two windows is called in by the desk.

9.3. Urgent security updates may be pushed outside the window. The desk warns the shift leads first, and the update waits for the device to be docked.

9.4. Nobody updates a K7 by hand, from a memory card or from a cable.

9.5. Sites that work through Tuesday night arrange their docking so that each rack is full for at least an hour inside the window.

## 12. Cleaning and pests

12.1. The anteroom floor is swept at the end of every shift and washed once a
day, after the last van has left. FC-A is swept, never washed, because water
freezes where it lands.

12.2. The pest contractor visits on the second Tuesday of each month and on call
after any sighting. Bait stations are numbered on the wall plan in the office.
Nobody moves a bait station to make room for stock.

12.3. Birds roost under the apron canopy in the monsoon. The netting is checked
after every storm, and a bird inside the anteroom is reported to the shift lead
at once.

12.4. Waste is separated at the back of the shed: cardboard, stretch wrap and
general waste. Damaged product is never put in the general waste; it follows the
customer's instructions and the company's destruction rules.

12.5. The canteen is cleaned by the canteen contractor. Complaints about the
canteen go to the site manager in writing.

## 15. Review of this handbook

15.1. The site manager reviews this handbook every June and after any serious
incident, audit finding or change to the building.

15.2. Revision 3 of June 2026 recorded the new apron free window, the larger cell
and the earlier order cut-off, and moved the genset rules into their own
section.

15.3. Suggestions from staff go to the site manager at any time. Each one is
answered, whether or not it is taken up.

15.4. A revised handbook replaces every earlier copy in the office, the guard
cabin and the canteen on the day it is issued.

## 15. Repairs

15.1. All repairs go through the IT desk. The desk keeps a small stock of spare K7s and LP-40s at each site, so that a repair never leaves a rack short.

15.2. Devices are sent to the Korvex service centre in a padded case with a repair note. Nobody opens a device on site.

15.3. A repaired device is rebuilt from Fernguard before it is reissued.

15.4. A device that has been repaired three times in a year is retired.

15.5. The desk reports device faults by type every quarter to the site managers, so that a site whose scanners keep breaking can look at how they are used.

15.6. Repair costs are charged to the site's cost centre. A site that pays for many repairs is not punished for it; it is asked what is going on.

# Coimbatore DC site handbook

Everything that is particular to Coimbatore DC, in one place. Company-wide rules
still come from their own documents: temperature limits and excursions from
QCL-QA-SOP-17, dock booking from QCL-OPS-DOCK-03, driver hours from the Driver
Hours and Road Safety Policy. Where this handbook and a company-wide rule seem
to differ, ask the DC manager before acting, and do not assume the handbook
wins. What follows is how those rules are carried out on this site, with this
building, these people and this weather.

6.4. The two-person figure is lower at Coimbatore than elsewhere because the
path from the shed to the apron crosses the wash pad, which is wet for most of
the day.

6.5. Dry ice never goes into CBE-PHARMA, never into the closed dairy room, and
never into a cab. Unused pellets go back to the chest in the same shift.

## 13. Gaps in the cover

13.1. The policy does not pay for every loss. The main things it will not pay for are: loss caused by delay alone; ordinary leakage, shrinkage and wear; loss caused by the nature of the goods themselves; packing that was not fit for the journey when the consignor packed it; war and nuclear risks; and any loss caused deliberately by Quillfern staff.

13.2. Delay deserves its own sentence because it is so often argued. A load that arrives late, even through no fault of ours and even when the lateness spoiled it, is not a claim under TPC. A load that arrives late and is rejected by the customer for being late is not a claim either. If the delay was caused by an insured event — a crash, a fire, a four-hour stoppage of the machinery — the claim is for that event, not for the delay.

13.3. Strikes, riots and civil commotion, known in the policy wording as SRCC, are covered from 2026 by an endorsement. A load damaged when a road blockade turned violent is therefore covered; a load spoiled because a blockade kept it standing for a day is not, for the reason in 13.2.

13.4. Theft by the driver of a hired vehicle is covered only where the vendor's own driver details were checked at the gate as the hiring rules require. Theft by a driver whose identity was never checked is a gap.

13.5. Where the desk is unsure whether a loss falls into a gap, it intimates the claim anyway and lets the insurer decide.

## 16. Tolls and road charges

16.1. Every owned reefer carries an electronic toll tag registered to Quillfern.
The tag balance is topped up by Fleet Control; drivers never pay a toll in cash
unless the tag reader at the plaza has failed.

16.2. A cash toll is paid only against a printed receipt, which goes into the
trip bag. A handwritten receipt is accepted only when the plaza staff sign and
stamp it.

16.3. A tag that shows a low balance at a plaza is reported to Fleet Control
while parked, and Fleet Control tops it up before the next plaza.

16.4. Hired trucks use their own tags. Quillfern does not refund a hired truck's
tolls unless the purchase order says so.

16.5. Road charges at state borders and permit fees are paid by Fleet Control in
advance for owned reefers. A driver asked for money at a border that was not on
the dispatch note calls Fleet Control before paying anything.

## 8. Heavy days on the road

8.1. The insurer's exposure on any single vehicle is capped. The most it will pay for all goods on one vehicle on one trip is Rs. 1.2 crore, however many consignments are on board.

8.2. A full vaccine load easily goes past that figure, and so does a frozen load of premium seafood. Any dispatch whose total declared value on one vehicle is above Rs. 1.2 crore is declared to the broker in writing at least 48 hours before the vehicle leaves. The broker then gets the insurer's agreement to a higher figure for that trip, or tells us to split the load.

8.3. Fleet planners check the declared value of every pharma critical and every high-value frozen load when they build the week's plan, and send the list of trips over the figure to the claims desk on Thursday.

8.4. A trip that goes over the figure without a declaration is still covered up to Rs. 1.2 crore. Anything above that is uninsured, and the site manager who allowed the load explains why in writing.

8.5. Splitting a load costs a second vehicle and a second crew. Planners should prefer splitting to asking for a higher figure only where the second vehicle is already on the road; the broker's higher figure usually costs less than an empty run.

## 1. Scope

1.1. The policy applies to owned reefers, hired reefers, support vans, escort
cars used for pharma critical movement, and any vehicle carrying Quillfern staff
between a DC, customer site, toll plaza, hotel, or repair yard.

1.2. A driver is on duty from the first required report at gate, yard, hotel, or
customer premises until the vehicle is parked, keys are handed over or secured,
documents are deposited, and the driver is released by Fleet Control.

1.3. A customer request, delayed dock slot, vaccine urgency, milk spoilage risk,
or senior manager's impatience does not cancel this policy. NO LOAD IS WORTH A
LIFE.

## 10. Hired trucks and their drivers

10.1. A hired-truck vendor is on the approved list before the first booking, and
each of its drivers signs the policy acknowledgement at the gate before loading.

10.2. Hired trucks carry their own fuel. Quillfern fuel cards are never given to
hired drivers.

10.3. Hired trucks are sealed with cable seals. Their drivers are shown the seal
routine at the gate by the shift lead.

10.4. A hired truck without a working temperature display is not loaded with
cold-chain stock, whatever the vendor promises about a repair on the way.

10.5. Vendors are reviewed every quarter on arrival times, refused loads,
exceptions and any safety concern raised by a DC.

# Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy

This policy is in force from 1 May 2026 for all Quillfern employees, contracted
drivers, and hired-truck drivers operating under a Quillfern dispatch note. The
frontmatter says draft because HR has not migrated the policy library; it is not
a licence to ignore the clauses below.

## 18. Review of this manual

18.1. The Fleet head reviews this manual every April, alongside the annual review
of the Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy, and sooner after any crash or serious
exception that shows a gap in it.

18.2. Drivers and controllers send suggested changes to Fleet Control at any
time. Suggestions are read at the next Nagpur driver meeting.

18.3. A revised manual replaces every earlier copy at the Fleet Control desk, the
gate cabins and the driver rest room on the day it is issued.

## 6. Hired trucks

6.1. Hired-truck providers must receive this policy with the purchase order.
Their drivers must sign the one-page acknowledgement at the gate before loading.

6.2. A hired truck without a signed acknowledgement may be used only after the
Fleet head approves in writing. The approval must name the customer, route, and
reason.

6.3. Hired trucks may not carry pharma critical stock at night unless the vendor
has provided two drivers or Fleet head written approval.

# Fleet Operations Manual

The working manual for Fleet Control, fleet planners, owned-reefer drivers and
the managers of hired-truck vendors. It says how the fleet is run day to day. It
does not restate the driver hours limits, the temperature limits or the dock
booking rules; those have their own documents, and this manual points to them.

## 3. The calendar

3.1. The apprenticeship runs as one continuous programme with no break between the classroom and the floor. Months one to six are mostly in the workshop; months seven onwards are mostly on site, with a day a week back at Waluj.

3.2. From the January 2026 intake the programme lasts 18 months; the 2024 and 2025 intakes served 24. The shorter programme was possible because the workshop now has its own reefer body, cold room and generator, so that practical work no longer waits for a site to lend equipment.

3.3. Apprentices join in two intakes a year, so that there is always a senior group on site while a junior group is in the workshop. Each intake opens on the first working day of January or July and takes twelve trainees, no more. A thirteenth applicant who passes is offered the next intake rather than squeezed in.

3.4. Public holidays follow the Maharashtra list for apprentices at Waluj and the local list for apprentices placed at a site.

3.5. An apprentice who is ill for more than four weeks in a row may move to the next intake and pick up from the module they left.

## 13. Cabs, bodies and how they look

13.1. A Quillfern cab is kept clean enough that a customer's receiving clerk can
sit in it to sign papers. Food wrappers, bottles and bedding are cleared out at
the end of every duty day.

13.2. Nothing is stuck to the windscreen except the permits the law requires and
the Quillfern asset number. Stickers, pictures and hanging charms that block the
driver's view are removed at the takeover walk-round.

13.3. The outside of the body is washed at least once a week, and after any run
through a construction zone or mud. A body whose company markings cannot be read
is washed before its next customer drop.

13.4. Scratches and dents are reported, not painted over. Fleet Control books
body repairs in batches so that no vehicle is off the road longer than it needs
to be.

13.5. The cab card, the red sleeve and the fire extinguisher each have a fixed
place in the cab. A driver who finds any of them moved puts it back and tells
Fleet Control, because the next driver will look for it in its fixed place in a
hurry.

## 6. Who may use one

6.1. A K7 may be used only by a person with a login issued by the IT desk. Logins are personal; a shift lead does not sign in for a picker so the picker can start sooner.

6.2. Contract and agency workers do not get permanent logins. Agency staff on the scanners are some of the busiest users on a peak night, and each one is given a temporary sign-in for the shift at the shift lead's request to the desk. The desk issues them a day credential that stops working twelve hours after it is first used. A new one is issued for each shift worked.

6.3. Personal phones are a separate matter. Many staff would rather scan with their own phone than walk to the rack, and on the pilot some did. No personal phone may run the scanning app or hold a Quillfern login, even for one shift when a K7 has failed; the user takes a spare from the cradle rack or waits.

6.4. Customer staff and auditors may look at a K7's screen with a Quillfern user beside them. They do not operate it.

6.5. Trainees from the Waluj workshop use a K7 only with their trainer's login running, and only for the exercises in their module.

## 13. Placement

13.1. From month seven apprentices are placed at a site that needs them. Placements are decided by the engineering pool lead with the site managers, and apprentices are asked their preference first.

13.2. An apprentice may be placed at a site far from home. The programme pays for travel and lodging and allows one trip home a month.

13.3. A placement lasts until the end of the programme unless the site closes, the mentor leaves or the apprentice asks to move for a good reason.

13.4. At the end of the programme, Quillfern offers a technician's post to each apprentice who completes, at a site with a vacancy. Taking the offer is not compulsory.

13.5. The site manager writes a short report on each apprentice at the end of the placement, and the apprentice sees it.

## 11. Mentors

11.1. Each apprentice placed at a site has a named mentor, a qualified technician who has volunteered and been trained for the role.

11.2. The mentor signs the logbook each week, meets the apprentice for half an hour each fortnight to go through it, and reports to the workshop once a month.

11.3. Mentors receive an allowance for each apprentice they mentor, paid with their salary.

11.4. A mentor may have no more than two apprentices at a time.

11.5. An apprentice who has a problem with a mentor speaks to the workshop lead, who may change the mentor without asking for a reason.

## 16. Welfare

16.1. Apprentices are young and often away from home for the first time. Each intake has a welfare contact at Waluj, a member of the workshop staff who is not a trainer.

16.2. Apprentices may raise anything with the welfare contact — homesickness, money, a problem at the lodging, a problem with a colleague — in confidence.

16.3. The lodging used at each site is visited by the welfare contact before the first apprentice moves in.

16.4. Bullying, ragging or initiation rituals are not tolerated, on site or at the workshop, and are dealt with under the company's discipline rules.

16.5. Apprentices are paid their stipend during approved sick leave for up to four weeks.

## 15. Repairs

15.1. All repairs go through the IT desk. The desk keeps a small stock of spare K7s and LP-40s at each site, so that a repair never leaves a rack short.

15.2. Devices are sent to the Korvex service centre in a padded case with a repair note. Nobody opens a device on site.

15.3. A repaired device is rebuilt from Fernguard before it is reissued.

15.4. A device that has been repaired three times in a year is retired.

15.5. The desk reports device faults by type every quarter to the site managers, so that a site whose scanners keep breaking can look at how they are used.

15.6. Repair costs are charged to the site's cost centre. A site that pays for many repairs is not punished for it; it is asked what is going on.

## 3. Gate and apron

3.1. The gate is staffed round the clock. Every vehicle is logged in with its
registration, its seal number, the customer and the time, and logged out the
same way. A vehicle that leaves without being logged out is reported to the site
manager the same shift.

3.2. The apron takes nine vehicles. Brand owners often drop a trailer and take
the tractor away, collecting the empty trailer later; a dropped trailer stands
on the apron with its reefer unit running on the shore-power posts along the
south fence.

3.3. Reefer units are plugged into shore power within 15 minutes of a trailer
being dropped. A driver who leaves a reefer running on diesel on the apron is
asked to plug it in, and the guard notes the time on the gate log.

3.4. Detention on a trailer that a customer has dropped or sent is billed to
that customer, not absorbed by the site. The clock starts at gate-in; nothing is charged for the first three hours, and each started hour after that costs Rs. 900. On the invoice it appears as a wait-time line and is taxed in the same way
as one.

3.5. Until 31 March 2026 four hours were free. The window came down from 1 April
2026, when two apron bays were lost to the enlarged cell behind D3 and every
remaining bay became worth more.

3.6. The guard does not decide detention. The office works it out from the gate
log at the end of each day, and a customer who disputes a line is sent the gate
log entries themselves, not a summary of them.

3.7. Reversing onto D1 and D2 after dark needs a spotter with a torch. The apron
lights run from the site's own supply and stay on when the grid fails.

3.8. Trailers are never parked across the fire lane that runs along the north
fence to the plant room door. The lane is marked in red hatching and is checked
by the guard at every shift change.

## 7. Machinery that stops

7.1. A loss of temperature on its own is not an accident. Under TPC, spoilage caused by a failure of the vehicle's refrigerating machinery is paid only where the machinery stopped working for at least four consecutive hours. Spoilage after a shorter stoppage is Quillfern's loss, not the insurer's, unless the stoppage followed a collision, an overturning or a fire, in which case the ordinary accident cover applies.

7.2. The four hours are counted from the unit's own stop event in its controller log, not from the first temperature alarm and not from the time the driver noticed. A unit that stops, restarts, and stops again has two stoppages, not one long one.

7.3. The stoppage is proved by the controller's event log and the temperature record together. A driver's statement, however honest, does not prove it alone, and a phone photograph of a dark display is evidence only of the moment it was taken.

7.4. Fleet Control downloads the controller log as soon as a claim on refrigeration grounds is possible, before the unit is serviced. A mechanic who clears the fault log has destroyed the evidence, so workshops are told not to clear any log on a vehicle with an open claim.

7.5. Customers' stock that warmed during a long stoppage is still handled under the quality rules, whether or not the claim succeeds. A failed claim never leads to stock being released.

## 8. When the grid drops

8.1. The site has two gensets on a common panel. They start automatically when
grid power fails and carry FC-A, the cell, the plant room and the apron lights.
The canteen and the office air conditioning are not on the genset panel.

8.2. The gensets are test-run under load every Thursday at 10:00 for twenty
minutes. The run time, the oil level and any alarm on the panel are written in
the genset log.

8.3. The gensets share one day tank and one bulk tank. The tank is never allowed below 1,500 litres; the night lead dips it at 22:00 and orders a top-up from the listed bowser at 2,500.

8.4. During a long outage the night lead dips the tank every four hours and
writes each reading in the log. A bowser that does not arrive within four hours
of an order is chased by the site manager, not by the night lead.

8.5. Nobody refuels a genset while it is running. Fuel spills are covered with
the sand from the bin beside the tank and reported the same shift.

8.6. After the grid returns, the gensets run on for ten minutes before they are
shut down, and the panel is checked for any alarm that was raised during the
outage.

## 4. The first hour at the scene

4.1. People first. Nobody risks injury to protect stock, look at a seal or take a photograph. Where there has been a crash, the vehicle and the road are made safe and emergency services are called before anyone thinks about the load.

4.2. Once it is safe, the driver or the receiving shift lead photographs the vehicle from all four sides, the seal before it is cut, the inside of the body when the doors are opened, the damaged goods, and any label or batch number that can be read. Photographs carry the date and time, and they are sent to the site manager the same hour.

4.3. Nothing is moved except to protect people or to stop further damage, such as moving chilled stock into a working cold room. Whatever is moved is photographed first and written down.

4.4. Nothing is sold, given away, thrown away or destroyed. Damaged stock goes to quarantine like any other doubtful stock, and stays there until QA has decided and, where it applies, the surveyor has seen it.

4.5. Cut seals, broken packaging, the driver's paperwork and the temperature download are kept together in a bag marked with the dispatch note number. Police matters — theft, a crash with injury, a hijack — need a copy of the first information report, and the site manager asks for it on the day.

## 15. Review of this handbook

15.1. The site manager reviews this handbook every June and after any serious
incident, audit finding or change to the building.

15.2. Revision 3 of June 2026 recorded the new apron free window, the larger cell
and the earlier order cut-off, and moved the genset rules into their own
section.

15.3. Suggestions from staff go to the site manager at any time. Each one is
answered, whether or not it is taken up.

15.4. A revised handbook replaces every earlier copy in the office, the guard
cabin and the canteen on the day it is issued.

# Coimbatore DC site handbook

Everything that is particular to Coimbatore DC, in one place. Company-wide rules
still come from their own documents: temperature limits and excursions from
QCL-QA-SOP-17, dock booking from QCL-OPS-DOCK-03, driver hours from the Driver
Hours and Road Safety Policy. Where this handbook and a company-wide rule seem
to differ, ask the DC manager before acting, and do not assume the handbook
wins. What follows is how those rules are carried out on this site, with this
building, these people and this weather.

6.4. The two-person figure is lower at Coimbatore than elsewhere because the
path from the shed to the apron crosses the wash pad, which is wet for most of
the day.

6.5. Dry ice never goes into CBE-PHARMA, never into the closed dairy room, and
never into a cab. Unused pellets go back to the chest in the same shift.

## 14. Outside help

14.1. Several outside firms work in the building: the security contractor, the pest contractor, the cleaning contractor, the generator's service agent and the calibration laboratory. Each is approved by QA before its first visit and reviewed once a year.

14.2. The pest contractor visits on the first Thursday of each month and on call after any sighting. Bait stations are numbered on the wall plan in the QA office, and nobody moves one to make room for stock.

14.3. The cleaning contractor cleans the offices, the gowning room and the floors of the goods-in and dispatch bays. Chamber floors are cleaned by store staff only, so that nobody unfamiliar with the racking works in a chamber.

14.4. Refrigeration work on the chambers is done only by a firm approved under the company's arrangements for cooling-plant service partners. A technician who arrives without his induction card is not let in, however urgent the fault.

14.5. Calibration certificates from the laboratory are filed against the instrument's number in the document system. An instrument whose certificate is missing is treated as out of calibration.

## 10. Before tools come out

10.1. Any work that could start a fire, release refrigerant, expose live electrical parts, or put someone at height needs a written permit to work, issued by the shift lead before the job starts.

10.2. A permit for hot work — brazing, welding, cutting, grinding — is valid for one shift only, and never for more than eight hours. Work that runs past the end of the shift stops, and a fresh permit is issued if it is to continue.

10.3. Hot work needs a fire watch who stays for thirty minutes after the work ends.

10.4. The permit names the technician, the job, the place, the hazards, the controls and the time limits. The technician signs it, and signs it again when the work is finished.

10.5. A technician who starts work before the permit is issued is sent off site, and the partner is told the same day.

## 15. Customer audits

15.1. Customers may audit the store on ten working days' notice, and for cause at shorter notice. The RP or the QA lead hosts every audit; the store manager joins for the operational parts.

15.2. An auditor may see any record about the customer's own stock and any part of the building. An auditor may not see another customer's stock records or another customer's audit reports.

15.3. The store answers each audit finding within 20 working days with a corrective action, an owner and a date. Answers are written by the QA lead and signed by the RP.

15.4. Findings from customer audits are added to the store's own corrective action register, so that one customer's finding fixes the problem for every customer.

15.5. A customer may ask to observe a mock recall or a self-inspection walk. The request is granted where the customer's own batch is chosen or where the walk does not expose another customer's records.

## 12. Passing work on

12.1. A partner may not pass any part of a Quillfern job to another firm without Procurement's written consent before the work is done. A firm that subcontracts without consent is suspended.

12.2. Consent is given only where the other firm meets the same category's requirements in this standard, including the papers in section 4 and police verification where section 7 requires it.

12.3. Specialist work that the partner cannot do itself — crane hire, scaffolding, a manufacturer's own warranty technician — may be brought in with the shift lead's agreement on the day, but the partner remains responsible for it.

12.4. Agency labour sent in place of the partner's own technicians counts as subcontracting.

## 10. On live units

10.1. On a live unit — a working reefer, a cold room with stock in it, a customer's freezer — an apprentice is never the only pair of hands. Live means anything holding product or able to start without warning, and it is the real kit apprentices are here to learn on.

10.2. One qualified technician supervises at most three apprentices on live equipment. On a pharma chamber the ratio is one to one.

10.3. Night work is part of the job later, not at first. No apprentice is put on a night roster before month nine, even with a supervisor. From month nine an apprentice may be rostered at night with a qualified technician on the same job.

10.4. Apprentices never isolate, lock out or restore power on their own until they have passed the electrical module, and never on a pharma chamber during the programme.

10.5. An apprentice who is asked to do something on a live unit that this curriculum forbids says no, and tells the mentor the same day. Saying no is never held against the apprentice.

## 11. Gas in, gas out

11.1. Category A partners recover refrigerant from our plant into their own recovery cylinders. Refrigerant is never vented, however small the quantity.

11.2. For every job that removes or adds refrigerant, the partner gives the site a gas record showing the cylinder numbers, the weights before and after, the type of gas, and what happened to recovered gas: reused in the same plant, sent for reclamation or sent for destruction.

11.3. The gas record reaches the site within seven days of the job. A job without a gas record is not paid until it arrives.

11.4. The site files the gas records with the plant's own log, so that the plant's history shows every gram that went in and out.

11.5. Leak checks on plant that holds more than the legal threshold of gas are done at the intervals the law sets, and the partner records each one in the plant log.

## 16. Waste and destruction

16.1. Product that cannot be supplied is destroyed by a licensed medical-waste contractor, against a destruction certificate that names the batch and the quantity.

16.2. Destruction is witnessed by a QA officer and one other person. Both sign the certificate, and photographs of the sealed waste containers are filed with it.

16.3. Product is never thrown in general waste, even a single vial, and never given away, sold for scrap or used for training.

16.4. Packaging from destroyed product that carries a customer's name or batch number is destroyed with the product, not recycled.

16.5. The destruction register is reconciled each month against the quarantine register, so that every unit that went into quarantine has either been released, returned to its owner or destroyed.

## 6. References

6.1. Category A and B firms give two references from customers for whom they have done similar work in the past two years. At least one reference is spoken to by phone.

6.2. A reference from a relative of the firm's owner, or from another firm under the same ownership, does not count.

6.3. Procurement writes a short note of each reference call and files it.

6.4. A bad reference does not automatically stop approval, but it is discussed with the firm and the note of that discussion is filed with the reference.

# Ammonia alarm at Nagpur: what to do

## When the site siren sounds

1. Stop forklifts and trucks where they are and switch the engines off. Nobody drives through the plant yard.
2. Leave by the nearest door that does not face the compressor house. The security guard brings the gate register.
3. Go to muster point M2 by gate 2, beside the windsock.
4. The shift lead counts heads against the gate register and the dock sheet within 10 minutes and phones the count to the plant operator on extension 215.
5. Nobody goes back for stock, a phone or a truck. Pallets left on a dock are dealt with afterwards under QCL-QA-SOP-17; product loss is a QA matter.

## 7. Leaving the building in a hurry

7.1. The Coimbatore cold block runs on packaged refrigeration units on the roof.
There is no ammonia on this site, so the ammonia cards used at Nagpur do not
apply here and must not be pinned up here.

7.2. Coimbatore has one site siren, and it means leave the building. It sounds
for fire, for a gas smell from the canteen cylinders, and for a refrigerant leak
alarm from a roof unit.

7.3. Everyone goes to assembly point CM-1, the coconut grove corner inside the
east gate. Nobody gathers on the south apron: that is where the fire tender
comes in.

7.4. The shift lead counts against the gate register and the Dockwise day list,
and phones the count to the DC manager. Drivers waiting outside the south gate
stay outside and are counted by the guard.

7.5. Nobody goes back into the cold block for stock. Pallets left outside a room
are dealt with afterwards under the SOP.

7.6. The all clear is given in person by the DC manager or, at night, by the
senior guard after the fire service leaves.

# Ammonia alarm at Nagpur: why M2, and why nobody goes back

## Why M2 and not the canteen lawn

Until 2024 the ammonia muster point was M1, the canteen lawn. In the July 2024 monsoon drill the windsock put the canteen lawn downwind of the compressor house for four of the six drill hours.
M2, by gate 2, sits upwind under the south-west monsoon wind and has a second
way out on to the ring road. M1 is still the fire muster point.

# Coimbatore DC site handbook

Everything that is particular to Coimbatore DC, in one place. Company-wide rules
still come from their own documents: temperature limits and excursions from
QCL-QA-SOP-17, dock booking from QCL-OPS-DOCK-03, driver hours from the Driver
Hours and Road Safety Policy. Where this handbook and a company-wide rule seem
to differ, ask the DC manager before acting, and do not assume the handbook
wins. What follows is how those rules are carried out on this site, with this
building, these people and this weather.

## 11. Canteen, lockers and shifts

11.1. The canteen opens at 05:30 and closes at 22:30. The contractor serves
breakfast, a lunch thali and evening tiffin. Drivers waiting for a slot may use
the canteen but not the lockers.

11.2. Lockers are in the annexe ground floor. Each employee has one locker and
one key. Night-shift lockers are opened with the spare key held by security,
signed out in the key register at the gate cabin.

11.3. Shift changes are at 06:00 and 14:00. The outgoing shift lead walks the
cold block with the incoming one and hands over the Dockwise day list, the
quarantine list and any open alarm.

11.4. Overtime is approved by the DC manager in advance. Staff do not stay on
past 22:00 to finish a load; the load waits for the morning shift.

11.5. The first-aid box is in the canteen, and a second box is in the gate
cabin. The nearest hospital with a casualty department is 6 km away on the
Avinashi Road.

## 9. Insulin without spare cold

9.1. Coimbatore holds no passive shippers, no gel packs and no conditioning
cabinet. The passive shipper pilot is at Nagpur only, and it does not extend to
Coimbatore until a later project is approved.

9.2. Because there are no shippers, insulin at Coimbatore is never staged on an
open dock beyond the SOP limit. Insulin moves from CBE-PHARMA straight into a
reefer body that is already at loading temperature, and the reefer waits for
the insulin, never the other way round.

9.3. A customer who asks Coimbatore for a shipper-packed consignment is told
that the site cannot pack one. The account manager may arrange for a
shipper-packed consignment to come from Nagpur.

9.4. Coimbatore does not stock blue-cap or white-cap packs of any kind, and does
not freeze packs in CBE-FROZEN for customers. A customer's own packs returned
with a consignment go back with the customer's return challan.
